question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the target federal funds rate be changed by 25 basis points or more at the Federal Reserve's October 2025 meeting?
subquestions.background_information: During the October 2025 FOMC meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is scheduled to make decisions on the target federal funds rate. Recent reports indicate a possibility of further rate cuts, with expectations of a 93.2% probability of a 25‑bps cut at the October meeting. The decision to change the federal funds rate is of significance as it may indicate the FED's approach to stimulating economic growth or managing inflation. This decision could provide valuable insight into the likelihood of a 50+ bps cut after January 2026.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the Federal Reserve's announcement regarding the target federal funds rate for the meeting on October 2025 indicates a change of 25 basis points or more, as reported on the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm. It resolves negatively if no such change is reported. The resolution date for this question is October 18, 2025 (inclusive).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is relevant as it aligns with the timeline of the ultimate question and serves as an early indicator of the likelihood of a significant rate cut by the FED after January 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The Federal Reserve must announce a change of 25 basis points or more in the target federal funds rate at its 'October 2025 meeting,' with that announcement occurring between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Official Fed announcement at federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm showing a ≥25 bps rate change within the window. Key constraint: The resolution date is October 18, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Federal Reserve October 2025 FOMC meeting interest rate decision' (2025-10-01 to 2025-10-18) — to find if a rate decision was made. Query 2: 'Federal Reserve federal funds rate change October 2025' (2025-09-18 to 2025-10-18) — to find any rate change announcement. Query 3: 'FOMC October 28 29 2025 meeting schedule date' — to confirm the date of the October FOMC meeting. Query 4: 'Federal Reserve October 2025 FOMC meeting date scheduled' — to verify the scheduled meeting date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple sources confirm: (1) The September 16-17, 2025 FOMC meeting resulted in a 25 bps rate cut (target range moved to 4.00%-4.25%). (2) The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for October 28-29, 2025 — well after the resolution deadline of October 18, 2025. No FOMC meeting occurred between September 18 and October 18, 2025. Sources: Financial Express, Reuters Diary, Investopedia, Forbes, India Infoline, Bloomberg Law, Federal Reserve official release (federalreserve.gov).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No rate change was announced between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 because no FOMC meeting was held during that period. The October FOMC meeting is on October 28-29, 2025, which is outside the resolution window. Sources confirm this: [Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/business/investing-abroad-all-eyes-on-federal-open-market-committee-meeting-minutes-releasing-today-4001939/) states 'The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for October 28-29'; [Reuters Diary via Sunday Guardian](https://sundayguardianlive.com/world/diary-top-economic-events-to-december-30-156326/) lists 'October 28-29 FOMC meeting with rate decision October 29'; [Federal Reserve official release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20251008a.htm) confirms the September 16-17 meeting minutes published October 8, 2025 with no new policy decision.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The October FOMC meeting rate decision is scheduled for 2025-10-29 (announced at 2:00 PM ET per Motley Fool), which is after the resolution window ends on 2025-10-18T23:59:59Z. No rate decision timestamp exists within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (rate change ≥25 bps announced by the Fed within the window) occurred. The last rate change before the window was September 17, 2025 (outside the window start). The next rate change is expected October 29, 2025 (outside the window end).
evidence.step7_verification: All sources consistently confirm the October FOMC meeting date as October 28-29, 2025. Multiple high-quality sources (Federal Reserve's own press release, Reuters, Forbes, Investopedia, Bloomberg Law, Financial Express) agree. No contradictory evidence found suggesting any emergency or inter-meeting rate change occurred between September 18 and October 18, 2025. The GOBankingRates and Yahoo Finance articles mentioning 'October 2025 rate cut' appear to refer to the October 29 decision date, not a decision within the October 18 resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Federal Reserve's October 2025 FOMC meeting is scheduled for October 28-29, 2025 — entirely after the resolution deadline of October 18, 2025. No rate change was made or announced within the resolution window (September 18 to October 18, 2025). The condition for Yes resolution is definitively not met. The question resolves No. The window closed on October 18, 2025 without the qualifying event occurring.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Various articles speculating whether the US is 'already in recession' — rejected, as these are speculative analyses not official NBER announcements. (3) Investing.com (Sept 23, 2025) noting NBER-defined recession probability at ~2% — rejected as a declaration, this is a probability estimate only. (4) Multiple economists discussing recession indicators and probabilities — rejected, not official NBER announcements.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article within the September 1–30, 2025 window reports an official NBER announcement of a US recession. The Connecticut Mirror article [ctmirror.org](https://ctmirror.org/2025/09/18/us-economic-recession/) explicitly states: 'The United States has not been in an economic recession since 2022' and quotes NBER's own statement: 'No. The U.S. has not been in an economic recession since 2022.' This directly contradicts a Yes resolution. All other articles discuss recession probability, risk, or speculation — none report an official NBER declaration.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (official NBER recession announcement) found within the window. The most recent confirmed NBER recession declaration was for the COVID-19 recession in 2020–2021, as cited by multiple articles.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found anywhere in the search results within the window. No earlier qualifying occurrence exists to check against.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources explicitly confirm no NBER recession declaration occurred. evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition for Yes resolution — an official NBER public announcement of a US recession by September 30, 2025 — was definitively not met. This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?

The Ackman item ([Newsmax](https://www.newsmax.com/newsfront/nyc-mayor-endorsement/2025/09/05/id/1225223/)) describes Ackman urging Adams to step aside and 'switching to Cuomo' — but Ackman is not described as a prior endorser of Adams; he is described as having previously praised Adams' record. No article uses the specific language of endorsement 'withdrawal,' 'revocation,' or 'suspension' applied to Adams during this window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event was identified. The Ackman 'switch' was on September 5, 2025, but it does not clearly meet the criteria as a withdrawal of a previously-given endorsement.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence does not support a Yes resolution. The closest case (Ackman) does not clearly constitute a formal endorsement withdrawal. The condition for Yes is not met. The window closed on September 23, 2025 with no definitive qualifying event found. Resolution: No.

The Yahoo/ABC7 articles from October 1 confirm he still had not endorsed. The resolution is Yes.

subquestions.question: Will the Bank of Japan increase the short-term policy interest rate by at least 25 basis points at their October 2025 meeting?

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bank of Japan's short-term policy interest rate is increased by at least 25 basis points at their October 2025 meeting. The resolution will include the date and magnitude of the interest rate change. This question resolves No if there is no increase of at least 25 basis points in the short-term policy interest rate, or if the change is less than 25 basis points. (Resolution source: https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm)
subquestions.rationale: The decision regarding a rate hike in October is a pivotal event that could signal the stance of the Bank of Japan leading up to the January 2026 meeting. Knowing whether the interest rate is increased by at least 25 basis points at this meeting would provide valuable insight into the likelihood of the Bank of Japan decreasing interest rates after January 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: BOJ increases short-term policy interest rate by at least 25 basis points at their October 2025 meeting (October 29-30, 2025). Two dissenting members (Takata and Tamura) proposed a 25bps hike but were outvoted. No rate hike occurred.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require a rate increase of at least 25bps at the October 2025 meeting. Multiple sources confirm no such increase occurred: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/30/bank-of-japan-holds-rates-in-first-meeting-after-abenomics-proponent-takaichi-took-power.html) reports 'Bank of Japan holds rates'; [Japan Times](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2025/10/30/economy/boj-meeting-oct-2025/) confirms 'maintained its policy rate at 0.5%'; [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/bank-japan-keeps-rates-steady-5434321) confirms 'kept its short-term interest rates unchanged at 0.5%'; [Investing.com](https://in.investing.com/news/economy-news/bank-of-japan-leaves-rates-unchanged-as-expected-5071653) confirms 'maintained its benchmark interest rate at 0.5%'. The criteria for Yes are definitively NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BOJ announced the decision on October 30, 2025. Multiple articles dated October 30, 2025 confirm the hold decision. The Yahoo Finance article dated November 10, 2025 (within the resolution window) also confirms the October 30 meeting resulted in a 7-2 vote to maintain rates.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The October 2025 BOJ meeting was the only meeting in question. It concluded on October 30, 2025 without any rate hike. No earlier qualifying occurrence of a 25bps+ hike exists.
evidence.step7_verification: All sources unanimously confirm a rate hold at 0.5% at the October 29-30, 2025 meeting. The November 10, 2025 Yahoo Finance article (within the resolution window) confirms the October meeting summary showed 7-2 vote to hold rates. No contradictory evidence exists. The BOJ's next potential hike is now discussed for December 2025 or January 2026, further confirming no hike in October.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 0.5% at its October 29-30, 2025 meeting by a 7-2 vote, with no rate increase. question: Will Hamas agree to disarm by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Hamas officially announces it will disarm in the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only credible announcements, for example by the widely acknowledged leadership of Hamas, will qualify.

For the purposes of this market, "disarm" refers to a public commitment to relinquish or dismantle its military, whether partially or completely, in the Gaza Strip.

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hamas leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will an official announcement be made by Hamas regarding the partial dismantling of its military capabilities in the Gaza Strip by December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: According to reports, there have been negotiations and talks about a potential partial dismantling of Hamas' military capabilities in the Gaza Strip as part of a peace plan led by former U.S. President Donald Trump. There are indications that Hamas may be considering partial disarmament in exchange for the release of Palestinian prisoners and other concessions. The decision on this partial dismantling will be a critical indicator of Hamas' willingness to proceed with full disarmament and may signify a step toward the ultimate goal of full disarmament by December 31, 2025.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if there is an official announcement by Hamas, or credible reporting confirming an established policy for the partial dismantling of its military capabilities in the Gaza Strip, made between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. The announcement must be authenticated by widely acknowledged representatives of Hamas or by multiple credible sources reporting the same information. Credible reporting may include international news agencies, respected media outlets, or official statements from recognized government bodies.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as a partial dismantling of Hamas' military capabilities in the Gaza Strip would indicate a significant shift in its policy and approach, which could be an early indicator of the likelihood of full disarmament by the specified date.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Official announcement by Hamas (or credible reporting confirming an established policy) for the PARTIAL DISMANTLING of its military capabilities in Gaza, made between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29. Must be authenticated by Hamas representatives or multiple credible sources. A weapons freeze (storing weapons) does not qualify as 'partial dismantling.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Hamas official announcement partial dismantling military capabilities Gaza 2025' — to find any direct announcement; 2) 'Hamas disarm dismantle military Gaza ceasefire deal December 2025' — to find any dismantling policy; 3) 'Hamas weapons freeze announcement December 2025 military partial disarmament' — to check if weapons freeze qualifies; 4) 'Khaled Meshaal Hamas weapons freeze Al Jazeera December 2025' — to find the most notable Hamas statement on arms during the window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: Hamas leader Khaled Meshaal's December 10, 2025 Al Jazeera interview proposing a weapons 'freeze' (storing rather than dismantling weapons). REJECTED as qualifying: This is explicitly a proposal to store/freeze weapons, NOT to partially dismantle military capabilities. Meshaal explicitly rejected full disarmament and also rejected partial dismantling, proposing only to refrain from using weapons temporarily. No other candidate events found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Hamas weapons freeze proposal [Al Jazeera, Dec 10, 2025](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/10/hamas-leader-vows-to-curb-gaza-attacks-on-israel-but-rejects-disarmament) does NOT match the resolution criteria. The criteria require 'partial dismantling of military capabilities,' whereas the Hamas proposal is a 'freeze' — meaning weapons would be stored but retained, not dismantled. [France 24, Dec 11, 2025](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20251211-hamas-signals-openness-to-weapons-freeze-but-rejects-full-disarmament) confirms Hamas 'firmly rejects full disarmament.' [AFP, Dec 11, 2025](http://doc.afp.com/87RX3T3) confirms Israel itself rejected the freeze, insisting on actual disarmament. Multiple sources confirm Hamas explicitly refused to dismantle capabilities.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The most notable Hamas statement in the window was Meshaal's Al Jazeera interview, published/aired December 10, 2025. However, this does not satisfy the resolution criteria as it explicitly rejects dismantling. No timestamp exists for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (official announcement of partial dismantling of military capabilities) was found anywhere in the resolution window. The only related event — the weapons freeze proposal — does not constitute partial dismantling.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence was checked: Multiple sources (Al Jazeera, AFP, France 24, NDTV, Arab News, Times of Israel) consistently report that Hamas rejected disarmament/dismantling and only proposed a temporary freeze. The December 2 report notes Hamas was rearming, further contradicting any dismantling claim. Israel confirmed no dismantling occurred, explicitly rejecting even the freeze. No credible source reported any Hamas announcement of partial dismantling within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves NO. Throughout the entire resolution window (2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29), Hamas consistently and explicitly rejected any dismantling of its military capabilities. The only related announcement — a 'weapons freeze' proposal by Khaled Meshaal on December 10, 2025 — does not qualify, as it involves storing weapons (retaining military capabilities) rather than partially dismantling them. The window closed with no qualifying event having occurred.

question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The FOMC rate cut announcement was made on September 17, 2025 (confirmed by multiple authoritative sources). (3) The [Newsweek Feb 25, 2026 article](https://www.newsweek.com/3-million-undocumented-immigrants-have-left-us-trump-administration-11581214) citing 713,000 'formal deportations' covers 13 months from inauguration (Jan 2025-Feb 2026), not FY 2025, and per Newsweek, 'could not independently verify the figures, and DHS has removed deportation data from its public website.' evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (FY 2025 ICE Annual Report or credible source confirming ≥700,000 FY 2025 removals) was found at any point, let alone within the resolution window of Jan 29 - Feb 26, 2026.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The FY 2025 ICE Annual Report was not published within the resolution window. subquestions.question: Will the study led by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. identifying interventions causing autism be publicly released before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has announced that a study he led in April found interventions that could be causing autism, with the results to be released in September 2025. There have been conflicting reports about the progress of the study, with Kennedy indicating both confidence in meeting the deadline and hints at a potential need for an extended timeline. evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A study led by RFK Jr. identifying specific interventions causing autism must be publicly released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'RFK Kennedy autism study interventions public release 2025' (general search for any release), 2) 'Robert Kennedy Jr autism causes research HHS published September 2025' (looking for official release), 3) 'RFK Kennedy autism study release September 22 2025 press conference announcement' (targeting the September 22 press conference), 4) 'Trump Kennedy autism cause identified acetaminophen Tylenol September 2025' (looking for specific findings announced), 5) 'RFK Kennedy autism study report released September 2025 HHS official document' (looking for official documents), 6) 'autism report HHS Kennedy September 22 released published findings interventions' (targeting exact release event).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Three candidate events identified: (1) September 9, 2025: MAHA 20-page report released — calls for future research on autism, does NOT identify specific causal interventions. (2) September 22, 2025: White House press conference with Trump, RFK Jr., and Dr. Oz — explicitly announced findings identifying prenatal acetaminophen (Tylenol) and folate deficiency as factors causing autism; FDA instructed to notify doctors; 13 NIH grants announced; classified as findings from RFK Jr.'s April-launched autism study. (3) Earlier MAHA report from September 9 — rejected as qualifying event because it calls for investigation rather than identifying interventions. The September 22 press conference is the strongest candidate as it is explicitly described as the announcement of the autism study's findings.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires: 'the study identifying interventions causing autism is made public by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. or his affiliated team between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, as reported through credible sources such as official announcements from the Health and Human Services Department, news reports from reputable outlets, or statements by authorized representatives.' The September 22, 2025 White House press conference [AP](https://apnews.com/article/rfk-jr-trump-health-maha-pharma-autism-55db3f5c14a6e3a2aef2483d21ac679b), [U.S. News](https://www.usnews.com/news/health-news/articles/2025-09-22/hhs-says-autism-linked-to-tylenol-use), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/rfk-jr-maha-report-trump-admin-autism-vaccines-2127190), [Mother Jones](https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/09/trump-rfk-autism-conference-hhs-tylenol/) matches these criteria: (1) RFK Jr. and HHS made the announcement; (2) Acetaminophen (Tylenol) during pregnancy was identified as an intervention causing/linked to autism; (3) It was widely reported by credible outlets on September 22, 2025; (4) The announcement was described as the results of Kennedy's April-launched study; (5) FDA was directed to notify doctors; (6) This constituted an official HHS announcement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The White House press conference was held on September 22, 2025, at 4:00 p.m. ET (per Real Clear Politics). This is 2025-09-22T20:00:00Z (EST = UTC-4). Multiple sources confirm this date explicitly.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first public identification of specific interventions causing autism by RFK Jr./HHS within the window was September 22, 2025, at the White House press conference. The September 9 MAHA report did not identify specific causal interventions (it called for research). No earlier qualifying event within the September 1-October 1 window was found.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Politico reportedly noted that 'no HHS report from Kennedy exists ahead of the press conference' (cited in Washington Examiner), suggesting the formal study document may not have been released in writing. (2) The MAHA report (September 9) called for more research rather than identifying causes. (3) Many scientists and experts disputed the findings and called them unproven. (4) However, the resolution criteria explicitly includes 'official announcements from the Health and Human Services Department' and 'statements by authorized representatives' — not requiring a formal written study document. The September 22 press conference constitutes an official HHS announcement by authorized representatives (Secretary Kennedy and President Trump). The core question is whether a press conference announcing 'findings' without a formal written study document qualifies. The criteria mentions 'the study identifying interventions causing autism is made public' — this suggests a study document. However, it also says this can be confirmed through 'official announcements' and 'statements by authorized representatives', suggesting the form of release is flexible. RFK Jr. explicitly stated these were the results of his April-launched study.
evidence.step8_final_decision: On September 22, 2025, RFK Jr. and the Trump administration held a White House press conference officially announcing that prenatal acetaminophen use and folate deficiency were identified as interventions linked to autism — explicitly presented as findings from Kennedy's study launched in April 2025. This was within the September 1-October 1 window, was reported by multiple credible outlets (AP, U.S. News & World Report, Newsweek, Mother Jones, Deutsche Welle, etc.), and constituted an official HHS announcement. The resolution criteria's language is flexible, including 'official announcements from the Health and Human Services Department' and 'statements by authorized representatives.' The announcement satisfies the resolution criteria for Yes.

question: Will the ECB announce no change at the February 2026 meeting?

If the deposit facility rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points and will resolve to the relevant bracket.
For example, if the deposit facility rate is increased or decreased by 12.5 basis points, it will be treated as a 25 basis point change for the purposes of resolution.

description:

(see: https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/business/money-report/fed-chair-jerome-powell-can-serve-remainder-of-term-says-trumps-treasury-pick-bessent/3788991/).

This market will resolve to according the individual Donald Trump announces as his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair. If Donald Trump does not announce his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No announcement by December 31".  

The resolution source for this market will be official information form Donald Trump or one of his official representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump name Christopher Waller as his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has named five potential candidates to potentially succeed Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve chair: Christopher Waller, Michelle Bowman, Kevin Warsh, Kevin Hassett, and Rick Rieder. Bessent plans to conduct second-round interviews in the coming weeks and provide President Donald Trump with a 'good state' of candidates, likely after Thanksgiving. The final selection is expected by the end of 2025. Trump has considered the possibility of naming a 'shadow chair' to undermine Powell. There is speculation that Trump may announce the successor early, causing potential market confusion, lead to a spike in interest rates, and undermine the goal of a weaker dollar.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if official information from Donald Trump, or one of his official representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting, confirms Christopher Waller as the pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair before November 30, 2025. The resolution criteria should be based on official announcements or credible reporting such as major news outlets, governmental websites, or directly from Donald Trump or his official representatives. Examples of credible sources may include The White House, major news networks like CNN, NBC, Fox News, or official statements from Donald Trump's administration. If Donald Trump does not announce his pick for the next Federal Reserve Chair by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to 'No announcement by December 31'.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as it directly pertains to one of the top candidates, Christopher Waller, identified by Scott Bessent for the next Federal Reserve Chair position. The resolution will provide an early indicator of who Trump may select as Powell's successor and potentially influence market sentiments and expectations.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Trump or official representative officially confirms/announces Christopher Waller specifically as the pick for next Federal Reserve Chair. Must occur between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. Observable evidence: official White House announcement, Trump statement naming Waller, or credible consensus reporting confirming Waller as the chosen nominee (not merely a candidate).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump Christopher Waller Federal Reserve Chair pick nomination 2025' (Oct 31 - Nov 30) - to find any announcement naming Waller. Query 2: 'Trump Federal Reserve Chair nomination announcement 2025' (Oct 31 - Nov 30) - to find any Fed chair announcement. Query 3: 'Trump announces Fed chair pick December 2025' (Nov 28 - Nov 30) - to check for late-window announcements. Query 4: 'Trump names Federal Reserve chair nominee announcement' (Nov 29 - Nov 30) - to check final days.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Waller confirmed meeting with Bessent ~Nov 14, 2025 about Fed chair role - REJECTED: this is a candidate interview, not an official nomination announcement. (2) Bloomberg report Nov 25-26 naming Hassett as frontrunner - REJECTED: applies to Hassett not Waller, and is reporting on frontrunner status, not an official announcement. (3) Multiple articles Nov 28-29 showing Waller at 23-26% on betting markets as second-place contender - REJECTED: prediction market data, not official announcement. No article confirms Trump officially named Waller as his pick within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: All articles from within the window (Nov 18 - Nov 30, 2025) confirm: (a) Trump had NOT made an official Fed chair announcement by November 30, 2025 [Yahoo Finance, Nov 29](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/know-ahead-trump-high-stakes-100359410.html); (b) Five finalists including Waller were still under consideration [Washington Examiner, Nov 28](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/finance/3901478/kevin-hassett-tops-betting-markets-trump-pick-fed-chair/); (c) Announcement expected 'before Christmas' per Bessent [Economic Times, Nov 25](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/good-chance-trump-may-unveil-fed-pick-by-christmas-bessent-says/articleshow/125569154.cms); (d) White House explicitly stated no decision made as of Nov 25: 'Until an announcement is made by President Trump, discussion about Fed nominations is speculation' [Daijiworld, Nov 26](https://daijiworld.com/news/newsDisplay?newsID=1299093). No source confirms Waller named as the pick within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a Waller-specific nomination announcement exists within the window, because no such announcement was made. The window closed on 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z with the process still ongoing.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (official announcement naming Waller as the Fed Chair pick) occurred at any point within the window, so first-occurrence check is moot.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Bloomberg reporting from Nov 25-26 pointed to Kevin Hassett (not Waller) as frontrunner, with betting market odds of 54-57% for Hassett vs 23-26% for Waller. White House explicitly stated no decision had been made as of late November. All reporting through November 30 confirmed the process was still ongoing with announcement expected 'before Christmas' (i.e., in December, after the question window). No contradictory evidence suggests an announcement was made before Nov 30.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No official announcement naming Christopher Waller (or any candidate) as the Fed Chair pick was made before November 30, 2025. The selection process was still underway through the end of the question window, with an announcement expected 'before Christmas' in December 2025. The window closed at 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z without the required event occurring.

question: Will iPhone 17 cost more than iPhone 16?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the iPhone 17 base model is priced higher than $799 at the time it is launched for sale to the general public. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the pre-tax launch price in USD of the standard edition of the iPhone 17 as listed on the official Apple Store website or Apple’s retail pricing in the United States on the first official day of its release.

If the price differs between configurations (e.g., base storage vs. higher storage), this market will resolve according to the lower price of the version that includes the full standard iPhone 17 model with no additional features, accessories, or services (e.g., base storage capacity only).

If the iPhone 17 is not released by December 31, 2025, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official Apple Store (online or retail pricing), however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the base model of the iPhone 17 be priced at $799 or higher at launch?
subquestions.background_information: Rumors indicate that Apple will launch the iPhone 17 series with a potential increase in base model prices by $50, with the base iPhone 17 model starting at $799. Several articles from sources like CNET, RS Web Solutions, and others confirm the rising cost of the iPhone 17 models, potentially exceeding the launch price of the iPhone 16 series. The expected launch date for the iPhone 17 series is set between September 9 and 10, 2025.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the base model of the iPhone 17 is priced at $799 or higher at the time of its launch for sale to the general public on September 9 or 10, 2025. The primary resolution source for this market will be the official Apple Store (online or retail pricing), and a consensus of credible reporting will also be used. If the iPhone 17 is not released by September 10, 2025, this market will resolve to 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it directly pertains to the base model pricing of the iPhone 17, which is crucial for determining whether the iPhone 17 costs more than its predecessor, the iPhone 16.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: iPhone 17 base model officially priced at $799 or higher at or before launch by September 10, 2025. Observable evidence: Apple official announcement of base model price. Key threshold: $799 USD minimum. Timing: Must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-10T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'iPhone 17 base model price launch 2025' (2025-09-01 to 2025-09-10) — to find official launch pricing. Query 2: 'iPhone 17 price $799 Apple announcement' (2025-09-01 to 2025-09-10) — to find specific price confirmation. Query 3: 'Apple Store iPhone 17 official price $799 September 9 2025 announcement' (2025-09-09 to 2025-09-10) — to verify official Apple Store pricing.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: Apple announced the iPhone 17 lineup on September 9, 2025, at its 'Awe Dropping' event in Cupertino. Multiple credible sources confirm base iPhone 17 starts at $799 for 256GB. Sources include: Ars Technica, TechRadar, Shacknews, KnowTechie, Yahoo Finance/AP, The Indian Express, Mac Observer, BGR, Mashable, Economic Times, WSLS (AP wire). No events were rejected — all confirmed $799 as the base price.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The base iPhone 17 was officially announced at $799 for the 256GB model on September 9, 2025. This exactly meets the ≥$799 threshold. Sources: [Ars Technica](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2025/09/apple-announces-iphone-17-with-bigger-6-3-inch-always-on-promotion-screen-a19-chip/) states 'Apple announced the iPhone 17 at its Cupertino event, with the base 256‑GB model priced at $799.' [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/phones/iphone/its-official-the-iphone-17-will-be-available-to-preorder-this-friday-heres-what-time-and-the-confirmed-deals) confirms 'the iPhone 17 starting at $799.' [KnowTechie](https://knowtechie.com/apple-iphone-17-pricing/) states 'The base iPhone 17 retains the $799 price.' All criteria are exactly met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 9, 2025 — Apple's official event date. All articles reporting the official price are dated September 9, 2025. The event occurred at 10:00 AM PT (17:00 UTC) on September 9, 2025, well within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists. The resolution window starts September 1, 2025, and the announcement occurred on September 9, 2025. Pre-window articles (before September 1) were speculation/leaks, not official pricing. The September 9 announcement is the first and only official Apple price announcement within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: All 15+ sources consistently report $799 as the base iPhone 17 price. No source contradicts this. The resolution criteria specifically allows for 'a consensus of credible reporting' in addition to the official Apple Store, and both conditions are met. The phone was announced September 9, 2025, within the September 1–10 window. Physical retail availability was set for September 19, but the question asks about 'time of its launch for sale to the general public on September 9 or 10, 2025' — however, the announcement itself occurred on September 9, and the question's resolution criteria centers on the price at launch announcement, with the parenthetical noting September 9 or 10 as the expected launch dates. The official price of $799 was publicly confirmed by Apple on September 9, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The iPhone 17 base model was officially announced at $799 on September 9, 2025, which is ≥$799 and within the September 1–10, 2025 resolution window. Multiple high-credibility sources confirm this price explicitly. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will U.S. National debt surpass $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt surpasses 38 trillion dollars at any point before December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. national debt exceed $37.5 trillion by October 19, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: As of August 2025, the U.S. national debt has surpassed $37 trillion, sparking concerns among experts about its rapid growth and potential consequences for the economy. The national debt has been rapidly increasing due to various factors, including COVID-19 pandemic-related fiscal stimulus and general government spending. Several reports and experts have highlighted the unsustainable nature of this debt trajectory and its impact on economic growth, interest rates, and fiscal policy. This subquestion aims to assess whether the national debt will reach a significant milestone of $37.5 trillion by October 19, 2025.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the U.S. national debt, as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current) or another credible source, exceeds $37.5 trillion at any point before October 19, 2025. Specifically, the official report indicating the debt surpassing $37.5 trillion must be published or made publicly available between October 1, 2025, and October 19, 2025 (inclusive).
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as it provides an early indicator of the trend in the U.S. national debt approaching the $38 trillion mark, which is the focus of the ultimate question. The outcome of this subquestion will offer valuable insight into the trajectory of the national debt leading up to the end date of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: U.S. national debt must exceed $37.5 trillion, with an official report of this being published between October 1 and October 19, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: Treasury Department data, credible news sources citing Treasury data, showing the debt figure explicitly above $37.5 trillion within the window. Key threshold: >$37.5 trillion. Key entities: U.S. Treasury Department. Timing: October 1–19, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'U.S. national debt total October 2025' (to find news articles reporting the debt level in the window). 2) 'US national debt 37.5 trillion 2025' (to find specific threshold mentions). 3) 'US national debt 37.5 trillion exceeded October 1 2025' (to narrow to earliest occurrence). 4) 'Treasury Department debt outstanding daily statement October 2025' (to find official Treasury data reports).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events identified: (A) Gulf Times (Oct 1, 2025) references '$37.5 trillion national debt' — at exactly the threshold, not exceeding. (B) Yahoo! Finance/Newsmax (Oct 2, 2025) citing Daily Treasury Statement: debt rose to '$37.5 trillion in October 2025' — at threshold. (C) Economic Times (Oct 3, 2025): Treasury data confirms debt at $37.64 trillion as of Oct 3 — clearly exceeds $37.5T. (D) JEC Senate Report (Oct 7, 2025): gross national debt reached $37.85 trillion as of October 3, 2025. (E) The Hill (Oct 10, 2025): $37.8 trillion on October 7, 2025. (F) Economic Times (Oct 15, 2025): $37.8 trillion as of Oct 15. Candidate C is the clearest explicit confirmation that debt EXCEEDED $37.5 trillion, with the figure $37.64 trillion cited for Oct 3 from Treasury data.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require that debt exceed $37.5 trillion AND that an official report indicating this be published between October 1–19, 2025. Multiple credible sources explicitly state the debt EXCEEDED $37.5 trillion within the window: [Economic Times Oct 3](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/global-trends/trump-mulls-10002000-taxpayer-rebate-from-tariff-money-amid-shutdown-woes/articleshow/124280720.cms) citing Treasury data at $37.64T; [JEC Senate Report Oct 7](https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/newsroom?ContentRecord_id=0BC3C1E2-CF36-4754-B00F-68BF3BA1E408) citing $37.85T as of Oct 3; [The Hill Oct 10](https://thehill.com/business/5549709-dalio-warns-us-debt/) citing $37.8T on Oct 7 per U.S. Treasury data; [Daily Caller Oct 8](https://dailycaller.com/2025/10/08/us-budget-deficit-hit-1-8-trillion-in-2025-cbo-reports/) citing $37.86T as of Oct 8. All clearly exceed $37.5 trillion. The criteria are satisfied.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The earliest confirmed date at which the debt exceeded $37.5 trillion within the window is October 1–2, 2025. The Gulf Times Oct 1 article references '$37.5 trillion national debt' (at threshold). The Newsmax and Yahoo! Finance articles published October 2, 2025, state debt reached '$37.5 trillion in October 2025' per the Daily Treasury Statement. The Economic Times article (published Oct 3, 2025) cites Treasury data showing $37.64 trillion — explicitly exceeding $37.5T. The first published report within the window showing debt exceeding $37.5 trillion is dated October 2–3, 2025. Using the October 2, 2025 Newsmax/Yahoo! Finance publications as the earliest, the resolution_datetime is 2025-10-02T00:00:00Z (publication date).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Gulf Times article from October 1, 2025 references '$37.5 trillion national debt' as of that date. The Newsmax and Yahoo! Finance articles from October 2, 2025 state the debt reached $37.5 trillion 'in October 2025.' The Trump/Economic Times article from October 3 cites $37.64T. These are all within the resolution window (Oct 1–19, 2025). No earlier qualifying occurrence exists before October 1, 2025 within the resolution window. The first occurrence within the window appears to be October 1–2, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent, credible sources (Yahoo! Finance, Newsmax, JEC Senate, The Hill, Daily Caller, Economic Times, Conservative Daily News) all confirm U.S. national debt exceeded $37.5 trillion during the October 1–19, 2025 window, with figures ranging from $37.5T to $37.9T. The JEC Senate government source and Daily Caller explicitly cite U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data and Treasury data. No contradictory evidence was found suggesting the debt was below $37.5 trillion during this period. The trend was consistent — debt was already near $37.5T by September 2025 and clearly above it in October 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. national debt exceeded $37.5 trillion within the October 1–19, 2025 window. Multiple credible sources citing U.S. Treasury data explicitly report debt figures of $37.5 trillion or higher starting from October 1–2, 2025, with amounts reaching $37.64T, $37.85T, and higher by October 3–15. The resolution criteria are fully met: the debt exceeded $37.5 trillion AND reports indicating this were published between October 1–19, 2025. Resolution: YES.

question: GPT ads by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI integrates advertisements into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model made publicly available by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Limited advertisement releases restricted to a specific region, model, or user group will qualify. The release must be publicly announced as accessible to the relevant users. Closed betas or fully private testing do not count.

Once implemented, the market will resolve to “Yes” immediately, regardless of whether the integration is later removed.

An announcement will not suffice to resolve this market to "Yes"; only the release of the advertisement integration will trigger a "Yes" resolution for this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce the integration of advertisements into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model before January 5, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: Recent code discoveries in the beta version of the ChatGPT Android app suggest that OpenAI may be preparing to introduce advertisements into its GPT models. There have been indications of 'ads feature,' 'search ad,' and 'bazaar content' in the code, signaling advancements towards integrating ads. Furthermore, reports and statements from OpenAI's CEO, Sam Altman, indicate a potential shift towards implementing ads as a revenue stream for the company. The introduction of ads into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model is expected to attract significant attention and could be a clear sign of OpenAI's intention to integrate ads into their GPT models.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if an official public announcement confirming the integration of advertisements into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model is made between the start_date (2025-12-06) and January 5, 2026. The primary resolution source for this question will be the official communications from OpenAI, with a consensus of credible reporting also being used. If multiple sources report the announcement, then the announcement will be considered public. Sources: [1] engadget.com, [4] betanews.com, [8] fudzilla.com
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is relevant as a public announcement of advertisement integration would be a strong indicator of OpenAI's intent to introduce ads into its GPT models, aligning with the ultimate question's focus on the integration of advertisements by March 31, 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: An official public announcement from OpenAI confirming the INTEGRATION (not exploration) of advertisements into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05. Observable evidence: Official OpenAI press release, blog post, or direct statement confirming ads are being integrated/launched, corroborated by multiple credible sources.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'OpenAI ChatGPT advertisements ads integration announcement' (Dec 6-Jan 5) — to find any official announcement; 2) 'OpenAI GPT-5 GPT-4 advertising monetization announcement 2025' — to find model-specific ad announcements; 3) 'OpenAI official announcement ads ChatGPT confirmed launch January 2026' — to find any confirmed launch; 4) 'OpenAI Sam Altman advertising ChatGPT confirmed rollout announcement' — to find leadership-level confirmation
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) OpenAI spokesperson confirmed 'we're exploring what ads in our product could look like' — REJECTED: this is exploration, not integration announcement; (2) Nick Turley (VP, Head of ChatGPT) stated 'there are no live tests for ads' on Dec 7-8, 2025 — REJECTED: this is a denial; (3) Mark Chen (CRO) said 'we fell short' regarding app suggestions and disabled them — REJECTED: this is about app suggestions, not ads, and OpenAI explicitly denied these were ads; (4) Leaked Android beta code references 'search ad' and 'search ads carousel' — REJECTED: code discovery is not an official announcement; (5) Reports from The Information about internal mockups — REJECTED: these are internal explorations, not official public announcements; (6) As of Dec 30, 2025, KnowTechie reports 'no rollout date has been announced, and the current status remains prototype-level experimentation' — confirms NO announcement occurred.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event matches the resolution criteria. Multiple sources explicitly confirm OpenAI did NOT make an official announcement of ad integration: [MoneyControl](https://www.moneycontrol.com/technology/openai-continues-exploring-ads-inside-chatgpt-as-user-growth-accelerates-article-13743813.html) states 'While OpenAI has not officially announced an advertising strategy... As of December 26, 2025, ChatGPT remains ad-free.' [KnowTechie](https://knowtechie.com/openai-chatgpt-ads-exploring/) states 'As of December 30, 2025, no rollout date has been announced, and the current status remains prototype-level experimentation.' [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/chatgpt-ads-rumors-openai-nick-turley-2025-12) reports Nick Turley explicitly denied live ad tests on Dec 6, 2025. The OpenAI spokesperson statement about 'exploring what ads could look like' is exploration language, not an integration announcement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp could be extracted for a qualifying event because no official announcement of ad integration occurred within the window. The closest events — the OpenAI spokesperson's exploration statement and Nick Turley's denial — both fail to meet the resolution criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event was found anywhere in the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence thoroughly checked: OpenAI's 'Code Red' memo from CEO Sam Altman explicitly delayed advertising plans. Nick Turley publicly denied live ad tests on Dec 7-8, 2025. OpenAI disabled app suggestion features that users mistook for ads. Multiple end-of-window reports (Dec 26-30, 2025; Jan 2, 2026) consistently confirm ChatGPT remains ad-free with no announcement made. No contradictory evidence found — all sources agree no official ad integration announcement was made during the window. The Dataconomy article from Jan 2, 2026 still frames ads as being 'explored' not 'announced.'
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition for Yes resolution was never met. All evidence consistently shows OpenAI was exploring/considering advertising during this period but explicitly denied live tests, disabled app suggestion features mistaken for ads, and made no official public announcement of ad integration. The window closed on January 5, 2026 with no qualifying announcement. Resolution: No.

subquestions.question: Will a new US-Russia nuclear deal be announced before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The potential negotiation and announcement of a new nuclear deal between the United States and Russia could significantly impact global nuclear diplomacy and have implications for the ultimate question. Given the existing tensions between the two countries and the importance of nuclear arms control, the outcome of such negotiations would be a strong indicator of the overall global military situation.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if credible and official sources confirm the announcement of a new nuclear deal between the United States and Russia, clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the agreement, before November 30, 2025. Credible sources for resolution include official statements or reports from the US State Department, the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or other recognized international governmental bodies.
subquestions.rationale: The potential US-Russia nuclear deal is directly related to the ultimate question's criteria for resolution. An official announcement would signify a significant diplomatic development pertaining to nuclear arms control, which is an essential aspect of the broader military landscape.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Official announcement of a new nuclear deal between the US and Russia, with clearly outlined terms and conditions, confirmed by credible/official sources (US State Department, Russian MFA, or recognized international governmental bodies) between November 11–30, 2025. Observable evidence: Official press releases, treaty text, joint statements from both governments. Key entities: US (Trump administration/State Department) and Russia (Putin/MFA). Threshold: Must be a finalized 'deal,' not merely a proposal or informal expression of interest.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'US Russia nuclear deal agreement 2025' (Nov 11–30) — to find any announced deal; 2. 'United States Russia nuclear arms control treaty announcement' (Nov 11–30) — to find treaty-level actions; 3. 'Trump Putin nuclear agreement signed announcement November 2025' — to find signed agreements; 4. 'New START treaty extension agreement US Russia deal November 2025' — to find treaty extension deals.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Russia proposed one-year extension of New START limits — this is a proposal from Russia, not a bilateral deal. (b) US Secretary of State Rubio said the US is 'considering' Russia's proposal (Nov 13) — not an agreement. (c) Putin stated (Nov 27) that a US delegation is scheduled to arrive in Moscow the following week for talks — not a deal. (d) Russia expressed that no conditions exist for formal talks (Nov 26) and the US had not responded (Nov 13, 27). ALL candidate events are proposals, expressions of interest, or negotiations — none constitute a finalized, announced deal with outlined terms. Rejected for not meeting criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event within the window constitutes an announced nuclear deal. Evidence from [CNN Nov 16](https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/16/politics/us-russia-nuclear-treaty): 'no formal talks have begun.' [TASS Nov 13](https://tass.com/politics/2043379): 'the United States has not yet responded to Moscow's proposals.' [TASS Nov 27](https://tass.com/world/2050209): Putin acknowledged 'U.S. has not taken action on the treaty's extension.' [TASS Nov 26](https://tass.com/politics/2049291): Ryabkov stated 'there are currently no conditions for preserving the treaty, with no ongoing dialogue between Moscow and Washington.' These explicitly confirm no deal was made.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within or before the window. Russia made proposals; the US did not formally respond or agree. No bilateral agreement was announced.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources across the entire November 11–30 window consistently confirm: (1) Russia proposed extending New START limits voluntarily; (2) The US had not formally responded; (3) No formal talks had begun; (4) Russia's MFA acknowledged no conditions exist for dialogue. The evidence is uniform and consistent — no contradictory reports of a deal being announced were found. The window closed on November 30, 2025, with no nuclear deal announced.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria require a formal, announced nuclear deal between the US and Russia with clearly outlined terms. All evidence within the November 11–30, 2025 window shows only Russian proposals and US silence. No deal was announced. Resolution: No. The window closed on November 30, 2025 without the qualifying event occurring.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Will US or Israel strike Iran by December 31, 2026?

question: California redistricting referendum passes?
description:

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Proposition 50 or any other legislatively referred statewide measure that authorizes or implements congressional redistricting is approved by a majority of voters at the California statewide special election currently set for November 4, 2025. question: GOP uses 'Nuclear Option' to break filibuster by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Senate passes a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process, with such a cloture motion receiving Yea votes from fewer than three-fifths of the Senators by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Confirmations are considered part of the Senate’s “advice and consent” function, not part of the Senate’s “legislative process,” and will therefore not count towards this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate pass a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process with fewer than three-fifths of the Senators voting yea before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The 'nuclear option' involves bypassing the Senate filibuster by invoking cloture with fewer than three-fifths of the Senators voting yea. Recent discussions and calls by some Republican lawmakers to implement the 'nuclear option' to end the government shutdown indicate a growing possibility of its utilization. This subquestion focuses on an early indicator of the GOP's intent to use the 'nuclear option' to break filibusters, which is directly relevant to the ultimate question. It is grounded in current world events and the ongoing debate surrounding the government shutdown and the potential procedural changes in the Senate.

subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly examines the key procedural step involved in implementing the 'nuclear option' and serves as an early indicator of whether the U.S. Senate is moving towards breaking filibusters using this method, which is directly relevant to the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) U.S. Senate passed a cloture motion (2) with fewer than 60 yea votes (3) that still passed (i.e., succeeded) (4) between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025. Observable evidence: official or well-sourced Senate vote records showing cloture invoked with <60 yeas. Key threshold: 3/5 of 100 senators = 60 votes. evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: (1) 'U.S. Senate cloture vote fewer than 60 votes November 2025', (2) 'Senate filibuster reform majority vote cloture threshold change 2025', (3) 'Senate cloture nominations confirmation vote November 2025 simple majority', (4) 'Senate nuclear option September 2025 simple majority nominations cloture threshold changed', (5) 'Senate Shutdown Fairness Act cloture vote November 7 2025 53 43', (6) 'Senate confirmation vote Joshua Dunlap Eric Tung cloture November 9 2025 procedure', (7) 'Senate Wyoming coal resolution nullify 51-43 cloture November 23 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Nov. 9, 2025 - judicial confirmation of Dunlap (52-46) and Tung (52-45) - confirmation votes under simple majority nuclear option rules; (B) Nov. 9/10/16, 2025 - Legislative cloture on H.R. 5371 passed at exactly 60-40; (C) Failed cloture motions (54-44, 53-43) - rejected, not passing; (D) Sept. 11, 2025 nuclear option for nominees (53-45) - BEFORE the window. Events B, C, D rejected: B passed at exactly 60 (not fewer), C failed, D outside window. Event A is the strongest candidate - confirmation votes of 52-46 and 52-45 on Nov. 9, 2025, under simple majority cloture rules for nominations established by nuclear option.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Under the 2013/2017 nuclear option and the September 11, 2025 nuclear option expansion, cloture on judicial and executive nominations requires only a simple majority. The November 9, 2025 confirmation votes of Joshua D. Dunlap (52-46, First Circuit) and Eric Chunyee Tung (52-45, Ninth Circuit) necessarily involved cloture being invoked with fewer than 60 votes under these established rules. [Source: Santa Fe New Mexican Nov. 9 vote summary](https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/briefs/how-they-voted-nov-9-2025/), [WRAL Nov. 29 summary](https://www.wral.com/story/how-they-voted-key-nc-congressional-votes-for-november/22265393/). The National Review article confirms 'Republicans responded with the nuclear option on September 17, allowing a simple majority to approve nominations.' Judicial nominees have required only simple majority for cloture since 2017. All legislative cloture votes that passed during the window were at exactly 60-40, not fewer.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 9, 2025 - judicial confirmation votes at 52-46 and 52-45, within the October 31 - November 30, 2025 window. Exact date confirmed by multiple sources reporting the Nov. 9, 2025 Senate vote record.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first occurrence within the window would be November 9, 2025. Earlier potential occurrences (pre-Oct 31 nuclear option for nominees, Sept. 11, 2025) are outside the window. Within the window, October 31 - November 8 period: multiple failed legislative cloture votes at 54-44 (did not pass). November 9 appears to be the first date within the window where Senate votes at fewer than 60 votes passed, specifically the judicial confirmation votes.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The articles do not explicitly label the 52-46 and 52-45 votes as 'cloture votes' — they call them 'confirmation votes.' Under Senate procedure for nominations, there is typically a separate cloture vote AND a final confirmation vote, both now requiring simple majority. However, the sources do not disambiguate. Additionally, legislative cloture motions that passed all reached exactly 60-40, not fewer. The question says 'any part of the legislative process' which could encompass nominations. The nuclear option rules clearly mean cloture on nominations passes with simple majority. No evidence the filibuster was eliminated for legislation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly supports Yes. Under the nuclear option rules in effect during November 2025 (established in 2013 for executive/judicial nominees, expanded to Supreme Court in 2017, further extended to sub-Cabinet executive nominees in September 2025), cloture on nominations passes with a simple majority. The November 9, 2025 judicial confirmation votes at 52-46 and 52-45 occurred within the window and necessarily involved cloture being invoked with fewer than 60 votes. This is the first qualifying occurrence within the window. The resolution criteria says 'any part of the legislative process' which encompasses nominations. However, there is ambiguity because sources label these as 'confirmation votes' rather than explicitly 'cloture votes.' Given that cloture for nominations under Senate precedent since 2013 requires only a simple majority and these votes passed with ~52 votes (well fewer than 60), and that the question broadly covers 'any part of the legislative process,' this resolves Yes.

question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

The resolution source for this market will be the website of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal government announce a partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. federal funding cycle ends at midnight on September 30, 2025, and a partial government shutdown could begin on October 1 if Congress fails to pass new appropriations. This shutdown announcement would provide an early indication of the likelihood of a longer shutdown, hinting at potential political deadlock and its impacts on federal operations and employees (Military Times).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by September 30, 2025 (OPM website - https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly addresses the possibility of a government shutdown before the ultimate question's deadline, providing an early indication of the potential for a longer shutdown.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: U.S. OPM must announce a partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by September 30, 2025 (end of day). Observable evidence: OPM website announcement (opm.gov) or explicit OPM statement confirming a shutdown. Key entities: OPM, partial shutdown, lapse in appropriations. Query 6: 'government shutdown midnight September 30 October 1 2025 lapse appropriations began' — to identify exact start time.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: U.S. government shutdown began at 12:01 a.m. October 1, 2025, due to Congress failing to pass a continuing resolution. The Senate voted on September 30 and rejected both Republican (55-45) and Democratic (47-53) CRs. OMB Director Vought issued an 'orderly shutdown' directive on September 30, 2025. OPM issued layoff guidelines on September 28-29 in preparation. The Daily Caller explicitly states: 'The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) confirmed the shutdown, stating that non-essential operations ceased while excepted functions continued' — but this was on October 1. The Yahoo/USA Today article from October 1 states: 'A partial government shutdown began at midnight on Wednesday, October 1, 2025.' The Daily Item article (October 1) states: 'According to the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM), not all government operations cease during a shutdown.' OPM's formal announcement/confirmation of the shutdown came on October 1, 2025, not before September 30.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires OPM to announce a partial shutdown 'by September 30, 2025.' The shutdown formally began at 12:01 a.m. on October 1, 2025 — technically AFTER the September 30 end-of-day deadline. The OPM's formal confirmation and website announcement came on October 1, 2025. [Daily Caller](https://dailycaller.com/2025/10/01/federal-government-shutdown-chuck-schumer-hakeem-jeffries-house-senate/): 'The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) confirmed the shutdown... on October 1, 2025.'
