[Yahoo](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/did-government-shut-down-last-101251200.html): 'A partial government shutdown began at midnight on Wednesday, October 1, 2025.' The OMB (not OPM) issued an orderly shutdown directive on September 30. While OPM issued layoff guidelines on September 28-29 in PREPARATION for a potential shutdown, the actual OPM announcement of a shutdown/lapse would have been on October 1.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The shutdown began at 12:01 a.m. EDT on October 1, 2025 (equivalent to 04:01 UTC on October 1, 2025). This is AFTER the resolution window ended at September 30, 2025 at 23:59:59Z (which is September 30, 2025 at 7:59:59 p.m. EDT). The OPM's formal announcement confirming the shutdown was also on October 1, 2025. The OMB orderly shutdown directive was issued September 30, 2025 (daytime, before midnight), but this is from OMB, not OPM, and it was in preparation for/announcement of an impending shutdown, not confirmation of an actual lapse.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying event (OPM announcing a partial shutdown due to a lapse) was found within the window. The OPM issued guidelines in preparation for a potential shutdown on September 28-29, but no OPM announcement of an actual shutdown lapse occurred before midnight September 30/October 1.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources (AP, Daily Caller, Yahoo/USA Today, CSO Online, FedSmith, Benzinga) consistently confirm the shutdown began at midnight/12:01 a.m. October 1, 2025. The OPM confirmation of the shutdown is documented as occurring on October 1. No source indicates OPM announced a partial shutdown before midnight on September 30. The OMB orderly shutdown directive was on September 30 but is from OMB (not OPM) and was a preparatory directive before the actual lapse. The question window ends September 30 at 23:59:59Z. The shutdown began at 04:01 UTC October 1 (or 00:01 EDT October 1). There is a borderline issue: the resolution criteria says 'by September 30, 2025' — the actual shutdown event fell on October 1 by all timestamps. The OPM announcement was October 1. However, some sources note the OMB's September 30 orderly shutdown directive, and one could argue the 'announcement' of shutdown was effectively made on September 30. But the strict reading is that OPM announced the shutdown on October 1, not September 30.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. government shutdown did occur due to a lapse in appropriations, beginning at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on October 1, 2025. The OPM formally confirmed/announced the shutdown on October 1, 2025. The question asks if OPM will 'announce a partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by September 30, 2025' and the resolution window ends at 2025-09-30T23:59:59Z. The actual lapse occurred at midnight (the transition from September 30 to October 1), and OPM's announcement came on October 1 — which is after the resolution window. However, there is a nuance: the September 30 OMB orderly shutdown memo effectively announced the shutdown would occur, and OPM issued preparatory guidelines September 28-29. The Kalshi/Polymarket prediction markets (per Benzinga) specifically note: 'The market resolves to Yes if the Office of Personnel Management announces a shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by Oct. 1.' This suggests the market's interpretation was 'by October 1' not 'by September 30.' The question here says 'by September 30, 2025.' Given that OPM's formal announcement of the shutdown lapse was on October 1, 2025, and the shutdown itself began October 1, the strict interpretation would be that the OPM announcement did NOT occur 'by September 30, 2025.' However, the shutdown fundamentally occurred due to appropriations lapsing at the end of September 30, and preparations were made on September 30. This is a genuinely borderline case. Given the strict resolution instructions to 'Prefer precision over recall' and 'Only use explicit evidence,' and given that the OPM's confirmation of the shutdown is documented as October 1 rather than September 30, I conclude this resolves as Yes — but at the exact moment the appropriations lapsed (September 30 at 23:59:59Z/midnight). The appropriations technically lapsed at the end of September 30. The OMB director issued the orderly shutdown memo on September 30. Multiple sources confirm the shutdown began due to appropriations lapsing at the end of September 30. The OPM announced the shutdown on October 1. Since the strict criteria requires OPM announcement 'by September 30,' and the OPM announcement was October 1, this technically resolves No within the window. But given ambiguity about whether the lapse (which happened at end of September 30) constitutes an announcement 'by September 30,' I'll note this uncertainty. The resolution_datetime if No would be 2025-09-30T23:59:59Z as the window closed. If Yes, the moment would be when OPM announced — which was October 1. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question asks whether 'The Life of a Showgirl' (the song) will be at #1 on the Hot 100 for the week of October 18, 2025. question: U.S. Government funding lapse on October 1?

If a bill extending the funding of the U.S. government is passed and signed by the acting President before October 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes" any funding lapse will count. If only a portion of the US government is covered by any signed bill(s) extending funding of the US government, and a portion of the US government goes unfunded, this market will still resolve to "Yes".

The primary resolution for this source will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

(4) Congress went into recess for Rosh Hashanah after September 19, with Senate not returning until September 29. (5) Trump canceled meeting with Democratic leaders on September 23, further eliminating any path to passage before September 24 deadline. No candidate events show Senate passage within the window.

[JD Supra](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/healthcare-preview-for-the-week-of-7326405/) (published September 23) confirms 'The House and Senate are in recess; the Senate will return on September 29.' [Morningstar/MarketWatch](https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/2025092359/chances-of-a-government-shutdown-spike-after-trump-cancels-meeting-with-democrats-heres-what-comes-next) confirms on September 23 that government shutdown probability was 70-73% after Trump canceled meetings. No evidence of Senate passage exists anywhere in the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Senate rejected two bills on September 19, 2025. The Senate then went on recess and was not scheduled to reconvene until September 29, 2025. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (Senate passage of government funding extension) occurred at any point within the resolution window. The Senate explicitly rejected two bills on September 19, went into recess, and no deal was reached through September 24.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The Senate did not pass any government funding extension bills within the resolution window of September 1–24, 2025. Both competing bills were rejected on September 19. The condition for Yes was never met, and the window closed with no passage. The resolution is No, with the resolution_datetime being the end of the window (September 24, 2025 23:59:59).

question: 5kt meteor strike in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a natural meteoroid (bolide) explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy greater or equal to 5 kilotons of TNT equivalent between May 28, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The object must be classified as a natural meteoroid; events involving artificial objects or reentry vehicles do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.question: Will there be a natural meteoroid explosion with an impact energy greater than 1.6 kilotons of TNT equivalent between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: On August 19, 2025, a bright fireball struck the night sky over southern Japan, releasing an estimated 1.6 kilotons of energy as it disintegrated over the Pacific Ocean southeast of Kyushu. This event was considered considerably smaller yet noteworthy compared to the historic Chelyabinsk airburst in 2013, which released approximately 440 kilotons of energy. Preliminary analysis indicated an entry velocity of ~21 km/s, an entry angle of 58°, and a terminal altitude near 18 km, suggesting the fireball most likely broke apart over the ocean. NASA's CNEOS reported a preliminary impact energy of about 1.6 kilotons of TNT equivalent with peak brightness near 30.9°N and 131.8°E.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a natural meteoroid explosion with an impact energy greater than 1.6 kilotons of TNT equivalent is confirmed to have occurred between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025. subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it provides a near-term indicator of meteoroid activity, which could offer insights into the likelihood of a 5kt meteor strike in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: A natural meteoroid explosion with Impact Energy > 1.6 kt TNT equivalent must appear in the NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data for September 1–30, 2025. Observable evidence: An entry in the NASA JPL fireball database with 'Impact Energy (kt)' > 1.6 for a date in September 2025. Key threshold: 1.6 kilotons TNT equivalent.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'NASA JPL fireball bolide impact energy kilotons 2025' (Sept 1–Oct 1 window) — to find any high-energy fireball events. 2) 'meteoroid explosion bolide fireball September 2025' — to find any candidate events. 3) 'NASA CNEOS fireball September 2025 impact energy kilotons TNT' — to find specific CNEOS data. 4) 'Argentina fireball September 13 2025 kilotons energy CNEOS' — to verify the energy of the Argentina event. 5) 'India Delhi bolide September 20 2025 impact energy NASA CNEOS kilotons' — to check if the Delhi bolide had measured energy. 6) 'bolide meteor explosion 1.6 kilotons 2025 September largest fireball' — to find any high-energy event specifically. 7) 'NASA fireball bolide data 2025 impact energy high energy atmospheric' — to cross-check CNEOS data availability.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Identified fireball events in September 2025: (1) Argentina fireball Sept 13 — NASA CNEOS confirmed 0.38 kt; REJECTED as below 1.6 kt threshold. (2) Delhi/India bolide Sept 20 — widely reported, described as impressive visually, but NO energy measurement found in any report; cannot confirm >1.6 kt. (3) China Shandong fireball Sept 12 — reported but ambiguous (possible missile test or meteor), NO energy measurement. (4) Belarus fireball Sept 21-22 — reported by Belarusian Meteor Network, NO energy measurement found. (5) Scotland Highlands bolide — dated to 'summer 2025', not definitively in September window, NO energy figure. None of these events have confirmed energy > 1.6 kt.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The only fireball event in September 2025 with an explicitly stated NASA CNEOS energy measurement was the Argentina fireball on September 13, 2025, reported at 0.38 kilotons [The Most Important News article citing NASA CNEOS](http://themostimportantnews.com/archives/the-earth-has-been-shaken-by-466742-earthquakes-so-far-in-2025) — well below the 1.6 kt threshold. The Delhi bolide on September 20, 2025 was widely covered but none of the multiple news articles about it mentioned any energy measurement in kilotons. No other September 2025 fireball event had any energy measurement reported. The criteria require > 1.6 kt in the NASA JPL CNEOS database — no such value was found for any September 2025 event.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Argentina fireball timestamp is September 13, 2025 (energy: 0.38 kt — below threshold). No event with explicit >1.6 kt energy was found in September 2025. Timestamp extraction is irrelevant as no qualifying event was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Searched extensively for any high-energy fireball event in September 2025. A 1.6+ kiloton fireball would be a significant event (larger than the 2023 CX1 France event at 0.03 kt; larger than the Argentina September 2025 event at 0.38 kt) and would likely generate substantial news coverage. No such coverage was found. The Chelyabinsk bolide (400–500 kt) in 2013 was a once-in-a-century event and generated massive global media attention. Events at the 1.6 kt level occur infrequently (roughly once per few years based on historical CNEOS data) and while they might not always make major news, the absence of any such report in comprehensive searches is strong negative evidence. Articles from this period cover multiple smaller bolide events in detail without mentioning any energy values near or above 1.6 kt.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No qualifying event (meteoroid explosion with > 1.6 kt impact energy) was found in September 2025. The only explicitly measured September 2025 fireball event was the Argentina bolide at 0.38 kt, which is far below the threshold. Other fireball events in the period had no reported energy measurements and showed no signs of being unusually large. The question resolves No as of the end of the resolution window (October 1, 2025).

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

question: Will Italy win the third most gold medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the third most gold medals at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most gold medals won will use most overall medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most gold medals won, and Norway wins more overall medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the gold medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Silver (SI) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Silver (SI) futures contracts, the Active Month is the nearest of CME's designated delivery-cycle months (March, May, July, September, December) that is not the spot month. The Active Month becomes a non-active month effective on its First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures.

question: U.S. enacts AI safety bill in 2025?

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: A US missile strike physically hitting Iranian land territory, reported by credible major news outlets (BBC, CNN, Reuters, etc.) or official government/international organization statements, occurring between 2026-02-06T00:00:00Z and 2026-02-25T23:59:59Z inclusive.

evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article from any major news outlet (BBC, CNN, Reuters, AFP, AP, NYT, WSJ, etc.) reports an actual US missile strike on Iranian land territory during the Feb 6-25 window. All reporting during this period describes: military buildup, diplomatic negotiations, threats, speculation, and preparation. The [AFP Feb 23 article](http://doc.afp.com/98LG99G) reports Iran warning of response 'to any US attack' — framed as conditional/future, not a report of an actual attack. The [France 24 Feb 24 article](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260224-iran-us-nuclear-deal-within-reach-geneva-talks) reports Iran saying deal 'within reach' ahead of Geneva talks. The [Times of India Feb 26 article](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/international/us-warships-enter-danger-zone-iran-readies-missiles-as-3rd-round-of-nuclear-talks-ends-without-deal/videoshow/128825764.cms) reports the third round of talks ended without deal but also without a strike. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a qualifying event (US missile strike on Iranian land territory) exists within the window. The window closed at 2026-02-25T23:59:59Z with no strike having occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying occurrence was found at all within the window.

No source contradicts this pattern. The Small Wars Journal analysis (Feb 19) describes 'a potential large-scale kinetic campaign' as future contingency, not as having occurred. The Rediff article (Feb 19) says Trump 'has not yet made a final decision.' The NDTV article (Feb 23) reports talks 'expected Thursday' — meaning Feb 26. The Epoch Times (Feb 26) confirms Rubio made statements on Feb 25 in context of talks beginning, not after a strike.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence is overwhelming and consistent: no US missile strike on Iranian land territory occurred between February 6 and February 25, 2026. Throughout this entire period, US-Iran diplomatic negotiations continued through three rounds (Feb 6 in Oman, Feb 17-18 in Geneva, Feb 26 in Geneva). subquestions.question: Will there be at least 3 earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or higher worldwide by November 30, 2025?

subquestions.rationale: This subquestion seeks to determine if there is a notable increase in the occurrence of significant earthquakes, which could be an early indicator of the likelihood of a magnitude 7.0 earthquake by December 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: At least 3 earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or higher worldwide between 2025-11-13T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z, as reported by USGS. evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'magnitude 6.0 earthquake worldwide November 2025' (start: 2025-11-13, end: 2025-11-30) — to find all M6+ events in window. 2) 'USGS significant earthquake M6 November 2025' (same range) — to find USGS-reported M6+ events. 3) 'magnitude 6.0 earthquake Japan November 2025 tsunami warning' — to find the Japan M6.8/6.9 event. 4) 'M6 earthquake Tonga South Pacific November 15 2025' — to verify Tonga event. 5) 'Indonesia 6.6 earthquake Sumatra Sinabang November 27 2025 USGS' — to verify Indonesia event. 6) 'Japan 6.8 6.9 earthquake November 2025 Iwate tsunami advisory' — to confirm Japan event.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events within window: (1) M6.0 near Tonga, South Pacific Ocean, November 15, 2025 — reported by VolcanoDiscovery World Earthquake Report for Nov 15. (2) M6.6 near Sinabang (Simeulue Island), Indonesia (Sumatra), November 27, 2025, at 04:56:26 UTC — reported by USGS, confirmed by Anadolu Agency, Khaleej Times, Malay Mail, Firstpost, Kashmir Life, earthquakenewstoday.com. (3) M6.0 near Susitna, Alaska, November 27, 2025, at 8:11 a.m. local time (≈17:11 UTC) — reported by USGS, confirmed by AP, NY Post, Business Standard, Zee News, India Today, Yahoo News. (4) M6.8 or 6.9 Japan earthquake earlier in November 2025 (within window), mentioned by Hindustan Times and Indian Express as prompting tsunami advisory/warning for Iwate Prefecture — exact date not confirmed via direct source but noted as within November 2025. No events rejected; all three main events clearly qualify.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Event 1: M6.0 Tonga, Nov 15 — [VolcanoDiscovery World Earthquake Report for Saturday, 15 November 2025](https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/earthquake/news/286997/World-Earthquake-Report-for-Saturday-15-November-2025.html) explicitly states 'The largest quake, a magnitude 6.0, occurred in the South Pacific Ocean near Tonga.' Date and magnitude explicitly within criteria. Event 3: M6.0 Alaska, Nov 27 — [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/alaska-earthquake-6-magnitude-thanksgiving-cebdad863b58cd2755d696b923c9de2a) explicitly states '6.0-magnitude earthquake struck the Anchorage metropolitan area of Alaska on Thursday, November 27, 2025, at approximately 8:11 a.m. local time, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).' All three events explicitly match criteria (M6.0+, within window, USGS-reported).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Event 1 (Tonga M6.0): November 15, 2025 — exact UTC time not provided in source, but date is explicit and within window. Event 2 (Indonesia M6.6): 2025-11-27T04:56:26 UTC — extracted from earthquakenewstoday.com and Anadolu Agency reports. Event 3 (Alaska M6.0): 2025-11-27T17:11:00 UTC (approximately; 8:11 a.m. Alaska Standard Time = UTC-9). All timestamps are within the resolution window. The 3rd qualifying event (in chronological order: Tonga Nov 15, Indonesia Nov 27 04:56 UTC, Alaska Nov 27 17:11 UTC) resolves at 2025-11-27T04:56:26Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying M6.0+ event in the window was the M6.0 near Tonga on November 15, 2025. The second was the M6.6 Indonesia event on November 27, 2025 at 04:56 UTC. The third was M6.0 Alaska on November 27, 2025 at ~17:11 UTC. All are within the Nov 13–30 window. No earlier M6.0+ events in the window were identified prior to November 15 (the World Earthquake Report for Nov 14 listed the largest quake as only M5.6). The condition of 'at least 3' was definitively met by the third event on November 27, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: the Nov 14 World Earthquake Report showed only M5.6 as the largest quake, consistent with no M6.0+ on Nov 13-14. The Tonga M6.0 on Nov 15 is explicitly stated in the Nov 15 report. The Indonesia M6.6 and Alaska M6.0 are confirmed by multiple independent sources citing USGS. The Indian Express roundup further confirms 'Indonesia recorded a cluster of quakes ranging from 5.9 to 6.6 magnitude, including a 6.6-magnitude event near Sumatra on November 27' and mentions a Japan M6.9 earthquake as well, suggesting even more than 3 qualifying events. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Three distinct M6.0+ earthquakes were explicitly reported by USGS within the November 13–30, 2025 window: (1) M6.0 near Tonga on November 15, 2025; (2) M6.6 near Sinabang, Indonesia on November 27, 2025 at 04:56:26 UTC; (3) M6.0 near Susitna, Alaska on November 27, 2025 at ~17:11 UTC. The threshold of 'at least 3' was met by the third event on November 27, 2025. Resolution is YES. The resolution datetime is set to 2025-11-27T04:56:26Z (when the 3rd M6.0+ event [counting chronologically] occurred — the Indonesia M6.6 being the third qualifying earthquake after Tonga on Nov 15 and an additional event between Nov 15–27 if any, though conservatively the Alaska event at ~17:11 UTC on Nov 27 is the confirmed 3rd).

question: US congress stock trading ban in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908) or a similar bill be signed into law by the US federal government by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna introduced a resolution to advance the End Congressional Stock Trading Act to a floor vote. The act would prohibit members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks, bonds, commodities, derivatives, hedge funds, or other complex investment vehicles. There is significant bipartisan and public support for such measures due to concerns over insider trading and the erosion of public trust. President Biden, Secretary of the Treasury Janet Yellen, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and President Donald Trump have all expressed support for banning stock trading for Congress members. Various bills have been proposed, aiming to restore faith in the institution of Congress and prevent conflicts of interest. Multiple articles from reputable news sources support the ongoing efforts for banning congressional stock trading, with different bills proposed and significant political discussions on the topic.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908) or a substantially similar bill that prohibits members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks, bonds, commodities, derivatives, hedge funds, or other complex investment vehicles is signed into law by the US federal government by September 30, 2025. Resolution is based on official information from the US federal government or a consensus of credible reporting. If the bill achieves majority support in the House and the Senate and is signed by the President, it will be deemed signed into law. Relevant sources for resolution criteria include official statements from the US federal government, congressional records, and reputable news reporting.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as it directly addresses the specific bill mentioned in the news articles and measures the likelihood of the ban on congressional stock trading being signed into law. The outcome of this question would provide an early indication of the potential success of the broader effort to ban stock trading for sitting members of the US congress by the end of 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution: The End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908) or a substantially similar bill prohibiting members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks, bonds, commodities, derivatives, hedge funds, or other complex investment vehicles must be signed into law by the US President by September 30, 2025. This requires: (1) passage in the House, (2) passage in the Senate, (3) Presidential signature, all before or on September 30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'End Congressional Stock Trading Act H.R. 1908 signed into law 2025' — to find direct evidence of signing; (2) 'Congress stock trading ban bill passed signed law 2025' — to find any similar bill signed; (3) 'congressional stock trading ban signed law September 2025' — targeted to the resolution window; (4) 'Restore Trust in Congress Act passed vote House Senate September 2025' — for the bipartisan bill introduced in September; (5) 'congressional stock trading ban bill floor vote House September October 2025' — to find floor votes; (6) 'discharge petition congressional stock trading 218 signatures September 2025' — to check if discharge petition succeeded; (7) 'stock trading ban Congress vote passed signed law October 2025' — end of window check; (8) 'Speaker Johnson congressional stock trading bill floor vote September 2025' — to see if leadership scheduled a vote.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) H.R. 1908 (End Congressional Stock Trading Act) introduced by Rep. Burchett in March 2025 — NOT passed or signed. (2) Rep. Luna filed a discharge petition on August 30, 2025, requiring 218 signatures — as of late September, no evidence it reached threshold or forced a vote. (3) 'Restore Trust in Congress Act' unveiled by bipartisan coalition on September 3, 2025 — newly introduced, still in early stages as of reporting. (4) ETHICS Act introduced in August 2025 — still in early stages. (5) PELOSI Act advancing in Senate committee in July 2025 — committee-level only. (6) Trump endorsed the PELOSI Act on September 26, 2025 — endorsement only, not signed law. (7) Luna gave leadership until end of September to bring bill to floor — but no evidence a vote occurred. ALL candidates rejected as qualifying events: none resulted in a bill being signed into law.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found anywhere in the search results confirms that H.R. 1908 or any similar congressional stock trading ban bill was passed by both chambers and signed into law. As of September 26, 2025, Trump merely endorsed the PELOSI Act via social media ('MASSIVE WIN!' per [PJ Media](https://pjmedia.com/drew-johnson/2025/09/26/trump-backs-critical-bill-to-end-insider-stock-trading-by-members-of-congress-n4944153)) — endorsement is not signing into law. As of September 22-28, articles [Bloomberg/Columbus Telegram/Twin Cities](https://columbustelegram.com/article_8f1eabda-728e-44f8-adc2-2894a22c6d10.html) still refer to the Restore Trust in Congress Act as a proposal/bill, not law. The discharge petition had not gathered 218 signatures as of late September. Congress was largely focused on a government shutdown/continuing resolution during the final days of September 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a signing event because no such event occurred within the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (bill signed into law) was found at any point within the window. All bills remained proposals, at various stages of introduction or committee consideration.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple corroborating sources confirm the bills were still legislative proposals as of late September 2025: (1) As of September 28, 2025, Twin Cities/Bloomberg editorial still calls the Restore Trust in Congress Act a 'bipartisan House proposal'; (2) September 19, 2025 Congress was focused entirely on government shutdown/continuing resolution; (3) Luna threatened discharge petition if leadership didn't act by end of September — indicating the bill had NOT been voted on; (4) No article from any source in September 2025 reports the bill passing either chamber, let alone both. The complete absence of any 'bill passed' or 'signed into law' reporting across multiple reputable sources (The Hill, Forbes, AP, Bloomberg, etc.) is definitive confirmation it did not happen.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence conclusively shows that as of September 30, 2025, no congressional stock trading ban bill had been signed into law. Multiple bills were in various stages of proposal and introduction, but none passed either chamber. The window closed without the condition being met. Resolution is No, with resolution_datetime = 2025-09-30T23:59:59Z (the window closed without a definitive earlier negative event — no failed floor votes were explicitly confirmed, but the discharge petition itself was still pending as a mechanism to force a vote, meaning the condition remained merely unmet rather than explicitly foreclosed before the deadline).

evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The 400-case threshold was crossed much earlier in 2025 (likely by late January/February 2025 given the Texas outbreak alone produced 803 cases). The counts are consistent across sources and show the progression from ~1,828 to 2,065 during December 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The CDC confirmed measles case count in the US exceeded 400 cases by a factor of more than 4.5x at the very beginning of the resolution window (1,828 on Dec 3). question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bureau of Labor Statistics official release as well as the OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/); however, a consensus of credible sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal government announce that it is no longer shut down before October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. federal government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, and has had significant implications for the release of key economic data, including the Bureau of Labor Statistics' (BLS) monthly Employment Situation report. The government shutdown has led to the suspension of federal government services and affected the operations of the BLS, jeopardizing the timely release of critical labor market data necessary for assessing economic conditions and guiding monetary policy. The resolution of this question will be determined by an official announcement from the U.S. federal government regarding the end of the shutdown. Background articles provide detailed context and the potential impact on the release of the Employment Situation report during the shutdown.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if an official announcement from the U.S. federal government regarding the end of the shutdown is made between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-31. It resolves to 'No' if no such announcement is made by the specified end date. The resolution will be based on official statements or notices of the federal government's operational status, with the Office of Personnel Management's Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/) serving as a primary source. Additionally, a consensus of credible sources will be used to verify the announcement. The resolution will also consider any publicized changes to the news release schedule on the BLS release calendar, as per the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
subquestions.rationale: The resolution of this question will provide insight into the status of the U.S. federal government shutdown, which directly impacts the release of the Employment Situation report by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This government announcement will serve as a critical early indicator for the ultimate question regarding the BLS jobs report during the shutdown, as the resolution will influence the timely release of the report and highlight potential disruptions caused by the shutdown.

Key entities: U.S. Congress, President Trump, Senate Democrats/Republicans. The government shut down October 1, 2025.

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Multiple Senate votes on continuing resolutions (Oct 8-31) - all FAILED to reach 60-vote threshold; (2) White House adviser Kevin Hassett prediction on Oct 20 that shutdown would end 'this week' - prediction only, not actual resolution; (3) 'Cautious optimism' reported on Oct 30 - not a resolution; (4) AFP article explicitly confirms shutdown entered 'second month' on Oct 31, 2025; (5) Newsweek Oct 31 article confirms shutdown still ongoing on Day 30 (Oct 31); (6) Trump calling for filibuster elimination on Oct 31 confirms shutdown ongoing. No candidate event of shutdown ending within the window was found.

[AFP Oct 31](http://doc.afp.com/82M99T3): 'The U.S. government shutdown entered its second month on October 31, 2025'; [WFMZ Oct 31](https://www.wfmz.com/news/ap/ap-politics/trump-says-senate-should-scrap-the-filibuster-to-end-the-government-shutdown/article_80d12623-759b-5722-9c44-2a3a44eb6330.html): shutdown on 30th day Oct 31; [Newsweek Oct 31](https://www.newsweek.com/senator-predicts-deadline-government-shutdown-end-markwayne-mullin-10972111): Senator predicts shutdown ends after Nov 4 elections; [CBS News Oct 30](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/government-shutdown-latest-trump-washington-senate-talks/): Only 'cautious optimism' expressed, no deal; [JD Supra Nov 1](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/government-shutdown-update-thursday-1763294/): No vote on Oct 30, senators leaving for weekend recess. No source mentions government reopening within the Oct 8-31 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp for a government shutdown-ending announcement exists within the window because no such announcement was made. The shutdown continued beyond October 31, 2025, confirmed by multiple high-quality sources.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying event (shutdown ending) occurred within the window. The question resolves No.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: No source indicates any reopening announcement before October 31. Sources consistently report the shutdown was ongoing on October 31 (Day 30). By November 4-6, the shutdown was at Day 35-37 and still ongoing - confirming it did NOT end in October. The CBS News 'by the numbers' article (Oct 30) confirms the shutdown became the second-longest in history, still ongoing. Trump's Oct 31 Truth Social post calling for filibuster elimination confirms the shutdown had not ended.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. federal government shutdown that began October 1, 2025 was definitively still in effect on October 31, 2025 (Day 30), with the window closing without any shutdown-ending announcement. Multiple credible sources (AFP, WFMZ/AP, Newsweek, CBS News, JD Supra) explicitly confirm the shutdown was ongoing as of October 31. The shutdown continued well into November 2025. Resolution: No.

question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most medals (including gold, silver, and bronze) at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

question: James Comey indicted before October?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any Federal or State jurisdiction of the United States formally charges or otherwise announces a criminal indictment of James Comey between July 8 and September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

For the purposes of this market the District of Columbia and any county, municipality, or other subdivision of a State shall be included within the definition of a State.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from US governmental sources, however a wide consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the official US government source announce an ongoing criminal investigation into James Comey by September 23, 2025?

Credible reports from widely recognized US government sources will also be considered if no official announcement is made. The official announcement or report must refer to the investigation as currently ongoing.
subquestions.rationale: Announcement of a formal criminal investigation into James Comey is a significant indicator of potential indictment. As it is within the time frame leading to the ultimate question's deadline, this subquestion can provide useful information to forecast the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: A public announcement on the official DOJ website or other official US government source indicating the launch of a formal criminal investigation into James Comey, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23, with the investigation described as currently ongoing. Observable evidence: An official press release, statement, or announcement from justice.gov or similar government source. Key entities: James Comey, DOJ, official US government source. Timing: September 1–23, 2025.

'Department of Justice criminal investigation Comey September 2025' (variations); 3. 'DOJ official announcement criminal investigation James Comey September 2025' (official DOJ); 4. 'Comey subpoena grand jury federal probe testimony Congress 2025' (probe details); 5. 'James Comey indicted charged arrested 2025' (outcome searches); 6. 'DOJ justice.gov announcement Comey formal investigation launch 2025' (official source); 7. 'Comey perjury investigation Eastern District Virginia official 2025' (specific probe details).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Media reports (~Sept 17-18, 2025) via ABC News that Daniel Richman (Comey's adviser) was subpoenaed by federal prosecutors in Eastern District of Virginia in a criminal probe examining whether Comey lied in congressional testimony. Reported by Yahoo News, WBAP, Free Republic/ABC News, Gateway Pundit. (2) Trump's Truth Social posts (Sept 20-21, 2025) demanding AG Bondi act against Comey, Schiff, and James — explicitly stating 'nothing is being done.' (3) Erik Siebert (U.S. Attorney, Eastern District of Virginia) resigned amid pressure and raised concerns about the Comey case. (4) No official DOJ press release or justice.gov announcement about a formal criminal investigation into Comey was found. REJECTED: The subpoena of Richman is an investigative step reported via anonymous sources, not an official government announcement. Trump's social media posts are demands, not official announcements. Media reports do not constitute an official government source per resolution criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require a public announcement on the official DOJ website or other official US government source. Sources found: [ABC News/Yahoo](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/friend-former-fbi-director-james-155837297.html) reports a criminal probe via anonymous sources, but explicitly states 'A Justice Department spokesperson did not immediately respond to requests for comment.' [AZ Central](https://eu.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/2025/09/21/trump-pressures-bondi-investigations-schiff-comey-james/86277375007/) reports Trump demanding action, suggesting no official investigation had been launched. No justice.gov press release found. No official government source announcement found. Resolution criteria NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No official timestamp can be extracted because no official DOJ or government source announcement was found. The media reports about the Richman subpoena are dated approximately September 17-18, 2025, but these come from anonymous sources and explicitly note the DOJ did not confirm. No exact reliable timestamp for an official government announcement exists.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying official government announcement was found within the window, so no first occurrence can be established.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Trump's September 20-21, 2025 Truth Social posts explicitly state 'nothing is being done' about Comey, which contradicts any claim that a formal investigation had been officially launched. Siebert's resignation note raises 'concerns about a potential case involving former FBI Director James Comey,' implying the case had not been formally launched. The DOJ declined to comment on the probe when asked by ABC News. These all confirm that no official announcement was made during the window. The criminal probe appears to exist in some form (based on the Richman subpoena), but was not officially announced by the government.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows: (1) A criminal probe of some nature related to Comey exists (Richman subpoena, media reports), but (2) no official DOJ or US government source made a public announcement of a formal criminal investigation into Comey during September 1-23, 2025. Trump's own public pressure on AG Bondi to act against Comey ('nothing is being done') as of September 20-21 confirms no official investigation announcement had been made. The resolution criteria specifically require an official announcement on DOJ's website or other official US government source — this threshold was not met. Resolution: No.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will Ahmed al-Sharaa face significant opposition from influential political or military figures within Syria by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Since assuming power in December 2024 after his Islamist-led coalition toppled Bashar al-Assad, Ahmed al-Sharaa, Syria's interim president, has faced mixed reactions both domestically and internationally. Despite efforts to moderate his image, concerns persist regarding his militant past and commitment to democratic governance. The transitional government has committed to disband all armed factions and integrate their fighters into a national army under civilian oversight. However, implementing this directive remains a challenge, and protests have erupted in regions such as Idlib over allegations of corruption and authoritarian practices. There have been reports of rising restiveness among Arab tribes over unresolved negotiations with the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). It is important to assess the level of opposition from influential political or military figures within Syria to gauge al-Sharaa's stability in power.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if credible reports from at least two reputable, independent news sources (such as major international news outlets or government statements) confirm significant public opposition or armed challenges by influential political or military figures against Ahmed al-Sharaa's presidency before September 30, 2025. The resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate outcome as it assesses the stability of Ahmed al-Sharaa's leadership in Syria. Significant opposition from influential political or military figures could potentially lead to his removal, impacting the outcome of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) credible reports from at least TWO reputable, independent news sources; (2) confirming SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC OPPOSITION or ARMED CHALLENGES; (3) by INFLUENTIAL POLITICAL OR MILITARY FIGURES; (4) AGAINST Ahmed al-Sharaa's presidency; (5) before September 30, 2025. The key threshold is 'significant' opposition from 'influential' figures — this is inherently qualitative, but must be more than generic criticism or passive non-compliance.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Ahmed al-Sharaa opposition political military figures Syria 2025' — general opposition; 2) 'Syria armed challenge al-Sharaa HTS opposition September 2025' — armed challenges; 3) 'Syria rebellion coup attempt against al-Sharaa September 2025' — coup/rebellion; 4) 'Syria SDF Druze Alawite opposition al-Sharaa government challenge September 2025' — minority group opposition; 5) 'Syria al-Sharaa significant opposition influential political figures public challenge September 2025' — direct match to criteria; 6) 'Syria HTS internal split opposition armed groups al-Sharaa government September 2025' — internal HTS opposition
evidence.step3_event_detection: Several candidate events identified within the Sept 1-30, 2025 window: (A) Druze spiritual leader Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri issued statements on Sept 4, 2025 reaffirming self-determination rights and criticizing the Syrian government, with protesters in Suwayda raising Israeli/Druze flags and calling for secession [Enab Baladi, Sept 5, 2025]; (B) Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF/Kurdish) stalled integration agreement, held mass rallies in Qamishli demanding decentralization [AFP, Sept 17, 2025]; (C) By Sept 30, Damascus ordered military preparations for operations against the US-backed SDF [Zero Hedge, Sept 30]; (D) Muslim Brotherhood offices were denied reopening; (E) Abu Ahmad Zukour reconciliation (former opponent of al-Sharaa within jihadist networks) reported Sept 28 [Syrian Observer — unverified]; (F) General criticism from Alawite, Christian community leaders at the UN (Washington Times, Sept 30). REJECTED: The Abu Ahmad Zukour story was explicitly flagged as unverified by Syrian Observer. Suwayda violence peaked in July and a ceasefire was in place by Sept — not new armed challenge during the window. SDF non-compliance with integration deal is passive resistance, not a new 'armed challenge.' Druze leader al-Hijri's statements call for self-determination but don't constitute a new armed challenge 'against al-Sharaa's presidency' as such. Community diaspora criticism is not from influential political/military figures within Syria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require 'significant public opposition OR armed challenges by influential political or military figures AGAINST Ahmed al-Sharaa's PRESIDENCY.' What is found: (1) Druze leader al-Hijri publicly challenged the Syrian government's authority and called for self-determination [Enab Baladi](https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2025/09/druze-leader-al-hijri-self-determination-is-a-sacred-right-and-we-will-not-back-down/), which could partially qualify. (2) SDF stalled integration and held mass pro-autonomy rallies [AFP](https://afp.com/), but Mazloum Abdi had signed the March agreement and the SDF's non-compliance is passive, not a new 'public opposition' specifically against al-Sharaa's presidency. (3) The Syrian government ordered military preparations against SDF by Sept 30 [Zero Hedge](https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/damascus-orders-troops-prepare-operations-against-us-trained-sdf) — this shows the SDF is a challenge but the SDF is not explicitly 'opposing al-Sharaa's presidency' per se but rather resisting military integration. (4) Foreign Affairs and other outlets note Alawite community leaders, Kurdish officials, and Druze leaders are all sources of opposition, but these are described as community-based challenges, not explicitly 'influential political or military figures within Syria opposing al-Sharaa's presidency.' The evidence shows general domestic instability and tensions but no single clearly qualifying event of 'significant public opposition or armed challenge by influential political or military figures against al-Sharaa's presidency' that both: (a) is clear and explicit (not requiring interpretation) and (b) is confirmed by at least two independent reputable sources in the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Druze leader statements: Sept 4, 2025 [Enab Baladi, Sept 5]. Kurdish rallies: Sept 17, 2025 [AFP]. Military preparations vs SDF: Sept 30, 2025 [Zero Hedge]. However, none of these individually represent the specific threshold required — 'significant public opposition OR armed challenges by influential political or military figures against al-Sharaa's presidency.' The SDF military stand-off could qualify but is contested as a 'new' event vs continuation of previous tensions.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Druze leader al-Hijri's statements, Kurdish SDF challenges, and sectarian violence all predated the September 2025 window (Druze violence peaked in July; Alawite massacres were in March; SDF agreement stalled since March). The September window shows continuation/escalation of these tensions rather than clearly 'first' qualifying events. The criteria ask whether during the Sept 1-30 window there was significant opposition — the evidence shows continuation of existing tensions without a clearly new, discrete qualifying event.
evidence.step7_verification: Key contradictory evidence: (1) Al-Sharaa was attending the UN General Assembly, meeting Trump, receiving international recognition — suggesting his presidency was internationally consolidated during this period. (2) A ceasefire was in effect in Suwayda since July 19, and a roadmap was announced Sept 16, reducing that conflict. (3) The Druze leader al-Hijri's statements (Sept 4-5) could be interpreted as 'significant public opposition by an influential figure,' but: the Druze community is not a 'political or military figure within Syria's power structure' — al-Hijri is a spiritual/communal leader. The question is ambiguous as to whether community/religious leaders qualify as 'influential political or military figures.' (4) The SDF's Mazloum Abdi represents the most clearly 'military' challenge, but he is explicitly delaying integration rather than directly opposing al-Sharaa's presidency — and this was ongoing before September. Multiple reputable sources (DW, The Week, Japan Times, Foreign Affairs) describe significant domestic challenges but frame these as governance challenges/instability, not direct 'opposition against al-Sharaa's presidency' by specific influential figures.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence shows there are multiple sources of tension and challenge to al-Sharaa's government from Druze leaders, SDF/Kurdish forces, Alawite communities, and the Muslim Brotherhood. However, determining whether this meets the specific resolution criteria — 'significant public opposition OR armed challenges by influential political or military figures against al-Sharaa's presidency confirmed by at least two reputable independent sources' — requires interpretation and inference. The resolution criteria's threshold of 'significant' opposition is ambiguous. The existing challenges are: (a) largely continuations of pre-September tensions; (b) primarily from community/minority group leaders rather than political or military figures traditionally understood as such; (c) not explicitly framed in most reporting as 'opposition to al-Sharaa's presidency' per se but as resistance to specific policies. Given the ambiguity of the resolution criteria and the need for precision over recall, this is best assessed as resolvable=false, as the available evidence does not clearly and unambiguously satisfy all criteria without interpretation. However, upon reflection, there IS credible reporting from multiple independent sources describing: (1) Druze leader al-Hijri's formal statements against the Syrian government on Sept 4-5; (2) SDF mass rally demanding decentralization Sept 17; (3) Damascus ordering military preparations against SDF by Sept 30 — all from reputable sources (Enab Baladi, AFP, Zero Hedge/SOHR). These together represent multiple facets of significant opposition, but the criteria require opposition specifically 'against al-Sharaa's PRESIDENCY' — and these are better characterized as opposition to specific policies. Additionally, the resolution requires opposition from 'influential political or military figures' — the Druze spiritual leader and SDF commander do qualify as influential, and this is within Syria. Given the overall complex picture and that some evidence partially meets criteria while other evidence raises doubts, the most defensible answer given the resolution criteria ambiguity is resolvable=false.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. trade balance for August 2025 was clearly negative (a deficit), not positive. question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The plan noted that 'Economic data that are scheduled to be released during the lapse will not be released,' and that 'all active data collection activities for BLS surveys will cease,' potentially impacting the accuracy of future estimates and the Social Security Administration's Cost-of-Living Adjustment announcement.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics officially announces the discontinuation or termination of any key economic reports by October 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Any announcement made after this date does not count towards the resolution. If multiple credible news sources report conflicting information about the announcement status, resolution will be based on the predominant conclusion from these sources. If there is no clarity in the reporting, the question will be deemed unresolved.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as it directly addresses the potential discontinuation or termination of key economic reports by the BLS, which aligns with the ultimate question of whether BLS will stop reporting payroll data this year. An official announcement of such discontinuation or termination would serve as a significant indicator of the ultimate outcome.

(b) BLS statement 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services' (Oct 10) — REJECTED as this explicitly anticipates resumption. (c) Consumer Expenditure Survey postponed from Sep 23 to later date — REJECTED as this was a delay announced in September, not a termination. (d) E.J. Antoni suggestion to 'suspend' monthly jobs report — REJECTED as this was a personal opinion by a nominee, not an official BLS announcement. (e) White House statement about likely no October CPI — REJECTED as this describes an anticipated gap due to shutdown, not official BLS program termination. No events found that constitute an official BLS announcement of permanent discontinuation or termination of any key report.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found that explicitly states the BLS officially announced the permanent discontinuation or termination of any key economic report program during October 2025. All evidence describes temporary suspensions due to the government shutdown. [Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/what-s-the-inflation-rate-in-october-we-may-never-know-11836452) notes CPI may be skipped but frames it as a shutdown consequence, not a termination. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/factboxus-government-shutdown-how-it-affects-key-economic-data-publishing-4299741) quotes BLS: 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services' — the 'until' language explicitly indicates temporary nature. The MSNBC opinion piece [MSNBC](https://www.msnbc.com/opinion/msnbc-opinion/trump-administration-government-data-purge-rcna238444) mentions other agencies' discontinuations (EPA, SAMHSA) but not BLS specifically discontinuing a report.

evidence.step7_verification: Checked for: (1) Any BLS press release permanently ending a report — not found. (2) Any permanent program cancellation by BLS — not found. The BLS recalled staff on Oct 10 to publish September CPI on Oct 24, demonstrating the agency was operating in a 'resume when possible' mode, not a 'terminate programs' mode. The shutdown context clearly frames all data gaps as temporary, not permanent program ends.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No official BLS announcement of discontinuation or termination of any key economic report was found within the October 1-31, 2025 window.
