Participating is defined as entering the game for at least one snap.  

If Travis Hunter doesn't participate in 4 games of the 2025-26 NFL Regular Season Game by December 31, 2025, this market will resolve to "No". 

The resolution source will be official information from the National Football League, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used. 

Note: Offensive snaps on plays in which there is a punt will not count towards the total.

subquestions.question: Will Travis Hunter play at least 20 total defensive snaps and play 19 or less total offensive snaps across the first 2 NFL games he participates in?
subquestions.background_information: Travis Hunter, a two-way star and the No. 2 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, aims to play both offense and defense in the NFL. There have been conflicting reports on how the Jacksonville Jaguars plan to utilize his skills, with discussions ranging from significant offensive workload to a balance between offense and defense. A successful performance in the first 2 games could be an early indicator of his usage.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Travis Hunter plays at least 20 total defensive snaps and plays 19 or less total offensive snaps across the first 2 NFL games he participates in. This will be determined using official information from the National Football League or a consensus of credible reporting. The start date for this question is 2025-09-01 and the end date is 2025-09-27. Official NFL data or a consensus of credible reporting will be used for the resolution.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is relevant because it directly assesses Travis Hunter's early performance and usage in the NFL, which could serve as an indicator of his primary role as either a defensive player, an offensive player, or both.

evidence.step1_decompose: YES requires: (1) ≥20 total defensive snaps AND (2) ≤19 total offensive snaps across Travis Hunter's first 2 NFL games. First 2 games are Week 1 (vs. Panthers, Sept 7) and Week 2 (vs. Bengals, Sept 14). Key threshold: 20 defensive, 19 offensive (combined over 2 games). The condition fails if offensive snaps exceed 19 total across both games.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Travis Hunter NFL snap counts offensive defensive 2025' - to find total snap data; 2) 'Travis Hunter Jacksonville Jaguars first NFL game snaps' - for Week 1 data; 3) 'Travis Hunter Week 2 Bengals snap count' - for Week 2 data; 4) 'Travis Hunter Week 1 Panthers 44 offensive 6 defensive snaps' - to verify Week 1 figures
evidence.step3_event_detection: Week 1 data (Panthers): NBC Sports reports '44 offensive snaps and 6 defensive snaps'; ESPN confirms '44 offensive snaps and 6 defensive snaps'; Jaguars Wire reports '42 of 66 total offensive snaps and adding six on defense'; MARCA reports '42 offensive snaps and six defensive snaps'. Multiple sources converge on 42-44 offensive snaps and exactly 6 defensive snaps in Week 1. Week 2 data (Bengals): NBC Sports: '42 defensive snaps vs. 39 offensive snaps'; Yahoo Sports: '39 defensive snaps and 42 offensive snaps'; ClutchPoints: '39 defensive snaps'; Yahoo Sports (another article): '43 defensive snaps' per PFF early data. Offensive snaps in Week 2 confirmed at approximately 39-42.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require ≤19 TOTAL offensive snaps across both games. Hunter played 42-44 offensive snaps in Week 1 ALONE ([NBC Sports](https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/travis-hunter-played-44-offensive-snaps-six-on-defense), [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46191682/jaguars-travis-hunter-says-2-way-start-solid-more-come)). This already exceeds 19 offensive snaps after just the first game. Combined offensive snap total across both games: ~81-86 snaps (42-44 in Week 1 + 39-42 in Week 2). The ≤19 offensive snap threshold is not met. The ≥20 defensive snap threshold IS met (6 + ~39-43 = ~45-49 defensive snaps), but BOTH conditions must be met simultaneously for YES resolution. Since offensive snaps far exceed 19, the question resolves NO.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The condition became definitively impossible after Week 1 concluded on September 7, 2025. By the end of the Panthers game, Hunter had already played 42-44 offensive snaps, far exceeding the 19-snap total allowed across both games. The game was played September 7, 2025 (Sunday). Using ISO 8601, this would be approximately 2025-09-07T23:59:59Z (after the game conclusion).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists — the question asks about the first 2 NFL games, and Week 1 is definitively the first game. After Week 1, the offensive snap limit (19 total) was already exceeded by Hunter's 42-44 snaps in that game alone.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality sources (NBC Sports, ESPN, Yahoo Sports, Sporting News, ClutchPoints, Jaguars Wire/USA Today) all consistently report Hunter's Week 1 snap count at 42-44 offensive and 6 defensive snaps. Week 2 data consistently shows approximately 39-43 defensive and 39-42 offensive snaps. There is no credible source suggesting Hunter played ≤19 offensive snaps in either game. The offensive snap counts are consistent across all sources. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is definitively NO. Travis Hunter played 42-44 offensive snaps in Week 1 alone, and approximately 39-42 offensive snaps in Week 2, for a combined total of approximately 81-86 offensive snaps. This far exceeds the ≤19 total offensive snaps threshold required for YES resolution. While Hunter did satisfy the ≥20 defensive snaps condition (~45-49 total), both conditions must be met simultaneously. The question resolves NO at the conclusion of Week 1 (Sept. 7, 2025), when the offensive snap threshold was already definitively exceeded.

question: Trump appoints special prosecutor for Epstein case in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump officially appoints, or announces the appointment of a special prosecutor, special counsel, or other independent prosecutor to investigate matters related to Jeffrey Epstein by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.  Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”
 
To qualify, the appointee must be explicitly tasked with investigating the Epstein case. A public statement from Trump, the White House, or the Department of Justice confirming the appointment will be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution regardless of when the appointment goes into effect. 

General statements of intent without a named appointee will not qualify. 

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from the Trump administration or a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration publicly announce the appointment of a special prosecutor or independent prosecutor specifically tasked with investigating matters related to Jeffrey Epstein by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Since former President Trump has shown a pattern of publicly pressuring for prosecutions and investigations of individuals he perceives as political opponents, including those involved in the Epstein case, there is a possibility that the Trump administration could publicly announce the appointment of a special prosecutor specifically tasked with investigating Jeffrey Epstein-related matters. The appointment of such a prosecutor could be seen as a significant step towards initiating a formal investigation into the Epstein case, which relates to the ultimate question of Trump appointing a special prosecutor for the Epstein case in 2025. This subquestion aims to capture an early indicator of potential official action related to the Epstein case, which could impact the ultimate question.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if there is a public announcement from the Trump administration or a consensus of credible reporting confirming the appointment of a special prosecutor or independent prosecutor specifically tasked with investigating matters related to Jeffrey Epstein between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. The primary sources for resolution will be official announcements from the Trump administration or a consensus of credible reporting.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it seeks to provide an early indication of official action by the Trump administration specifically related to the Epstein case, which could impact the appointment of a special prosecutor as outlined in the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Public announcement from Trump administration of appointment of a SPECIAL PROSECUTOR or INDEPENDENT PROSECUTOR specifically tasked with investigating Jeffrey Epstein matters, between Oct 31 - Nov 30, 2025. Key distinctions: 'special prosecutor' and 'independent prosecutor' are formal legal designations with specific independence characteristics, distinct from a regular U.S. Attorney assigned to lead a DOJ investigation.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump administration special prosecutor Epstein investigation 2025' - to find any formal special/independent counsel appointment; 2) 'independent prosecutor Jeffrey Epstein appointed November 2025' - to find any independent counsel designation; 3) 'special counsel independent prosecutor Epstein appointed Trump 2025' - to verify formal designations; 4) 'Jay Clayton special prosecutor independent counsel Epstein investigation' - to check if Clayton's role was characterized as special/independent prosecutor.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: On November 14, 2025, AG Pam Bondi appointed Jay Clayton (acting U.S. Attorney for SDNY) to lead a federal investigation into Epstein's ties to Democrats. REJECTED as qualifying event: Clayton was appointed as a U.S. Attorney leading a DOJ investigation, NOT as a 'special prosecutor' or 'independent prosecutor.' He is described consistently as a 'U.S. Attorney,' 'top prosecutor,' or 'federal prosecutor' — never as 'special prosecutor' or 'independent prosecutor.' No other candidate events found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The appointment of Jay Clayton does NOT match the resolution criteria. Multiple sources confirm: [The Hill](https://thehill.com/regulation/court-battles/5606452-epstein-democrats-probe-clayton/) describes Clayton as 'acting U.S. Attorney for SDNY'; [CNN](https://us.cnn.com/politics/live-news/trump-government-shutdown-news-11-14-25) describes him as 'United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York'; [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/jay-clayton-trump-epstein-probe-pam-bondi-pick-11051212) describes him as 'U.S. Attorney for SDNY.' Critics noted concerns that Clayton may report directly to the president, explicitly noting LACK of independence. A special prosecutor/independent prosecutor has formal independence designations under 28 CFR Part 600 or equivalent statutory authority — none of which applies here. The investigation was also politically directed by Trump (not independent), focused on Democrats rather than being a neutral Epstein investigation.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 14, 2025 — announcement of Jay Clayton appointment. However, this does not qualify as appointment of 'special prosecutor' or 'independent prosecutor.'
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence exists. The only relevant appointment was Jay Clayton on November 14, 2025, which does not meet the 'special prosecutor' or 'independent prosecutor' criteria.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm Clayton is a U.S. Attorney, not a special/independent prosecutor. The Raw Story and dnyuz.com explicitly note concerns about Clayton being 'directly accountable to the president,' contradicting independence. The Lawyers Guns & Money article calls the investigation 'nakedly partisan.' No source describes Clayton's role as 'special prosecutor' or 'independent prosecutor.' The question's criteria require this specific formal designation, which was not used. Laura Loomer had urged Trump to appoint a special counsel in July 2024 (per The Hill), but this never materialized.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Trump administration appointed Jay Clayton (acting U.S. Attorney for SDNY) to lead a DOJ investigation into Epstein's Democratic ties on November 14, 2025. However, this does NOT qualify as appointment of a 'special prosecutor' or 'independent prosecutor' as required by the resolution criteria. Clayton is a U.S. Attorney embedded within DOJ's regular chain of command, not an independently designated special/independent prosecutor. The resolution criteria are not met. Resolution: No.

The resolution criteria focuses on 'announcements confirming the upcoming release' — the foundational announcement pre-dates the window by 2 days, but extensive coverage, confirmation, and ongoing promotional activity (including Coinbase's and Cobie's X posts which remained public) was present throughout the window. All major crypto news outlets had published detailed stories about this by the start of the window (Oct 23).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The primary announcement (Brian Armstrong on X) was October 21, 2025 — before the window opens October 23. Furthermore, the original X post from Coinbase's official account remained publicly visible throughout the window. The criteria requires 'social media promotions or other public announcements confirming the upcoming release' to be 'publicly released' between Oct 23 and Nov 22. Since credible media reports confirming this were published within the window (Oct 23+), and the official social media posts remained accessible, this resolves Yes. The first occurrence within the window is October 23, 2025.

question: Will the Sanctioning Russia Act of 2025 (S.1241) be signed into law by December 31 2025?

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Sanctioning Russia Act of 2025 (S.1241) is passed by both the Senate and the House of Representatives in official roll call votes between 2025-10-22 and 2025-11-21. question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the global mean near-surface temperature for the year 2025 exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels?

Greenhouse gas concentrations have reached record highs, and there have been extreme weather events, including floods, heatwaves, and wildfires in 2025. The trend of rising temperatures and related impacts indicates the possibility of exceeding the 1.5°C threshold.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the global mean near-surface temperature for the year 2025 exceeds 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled 'Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)' under the column 'No_Smoothing' in the row '2025' (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.
subquestions.rationale: This indicator directly addresses the likelihood of 2025 being the second hottest year on record by focusing on the global mean near-surface temperature. Exceeding the 1.5°C threshold would strongly suggest that 2025 has indeed experienced exceptional warming

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: NASA GISTEMP 'Land-Ocean Temperature Index' No_Smoothing value for row '2025' must exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. Observable evidence: the specific NASA GISTEMP graph.txt file must show ≥1.50 for 2025. Key entities: NASA GISTEMP v4, pre-industrial baseline (~1880-1899 or similar), year 2025. The data must be published before the window closes (Jan 11, 2026).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'NASA GISTEMP 2025 global temperature annual mean' to find whether NASA released 2025 data; (2) '2025 global temperature record 1.5 degrees above pre-industrial' to find temperature values from all sources; (3) 'NASA GISTEMP graph.txt 2025 annual temperature No_Smoothing value' for specific NASA data; (4) 'WMO global temperature 2025 confirmed annual average'; (5) 'Copernicus 2025 global temperature 1.47 second warmest confirmed'; (6) 'Copernicus ERA5 2025 annual global temperature confirmed 1.47 1.5 second warmest'; (7) 'Yale E360 2025 second hottest Copernicus 1.5 degrees'; (8) 'NASA GISS 2025 global temperature release January 2026'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) WMO announced 2025 global average at 1.47°C — does not use NASA GISTEMP specifically, and is below 1.5°C threshold. (B) Copernicus/ERA5 reports 2025 as 'more than 1.5°C' above pre-industrial (Yale E360, Vancouver Sun) — this uses ERA5 dataset, NOT NASA GISTEMP. (C) WMO consolidated data release for 2025 was scheduled for January 14, 2026 — outside the resolution window. (D) NASA GISTEMP-specific 2025 data release: no evidence found within the window. Rejected: Copernicus ERA5 data is not the resolution source; WMO >1.5 statements often refer to ERA5 or multi-dataset averages.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criterion requires the specific NASA GISTEMP 'No_Smoothing' 2025 value to exceed 1.5°C. Sources found: [Earth 911](https://earth911.com/earth-watch/oops-we-did-it-again-2025-second-hottest-year-on-record/) cites WMO at 1.47°C. [WMO release](https://www.miragenews.com/wmo-to-reveal-2025-global-temperature-data-1599230/) is scheduled January 14, 2026 (outside window). [Yale E360](https://e360.yale.edu/digest/2025-second-hottest-year) reports Copernicus shows 2025 as 'more than 1.5°C' — but this is ERA5, not GISTEMP. [Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/environment/weather-bee-how-much-global-warming-to-expect-in-2026-101767427744290.html) reports WMO projects ~1.4°C for 2025 when December included. Multiple sources converge on ~1.47°C for 2025 using multi-dataset averages. No source explicitly states NASA GISTEMP No_Smoothing 2025 value.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: NASA GISTEMP 2025 annual data: no publication timestamp within window found. WMO consolidated release: January 14, 2026 (outside window). No timestamp for NASA-specific 2025 GISTEMP value release.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: NASA GISTEMP 2025 annual value was not found published within the window. WMO release scheduled January 14, 2026. No earlier qualifying occurrence found.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: ERA5/Copernicus reports 2025 exceeded 1.5°C (multiple sources). However, the resolution criterion explicitly specifies NASA GISTEMP, which is a different dataset with different methodology and baseline. Non-Copernicus sources (WMO multi-dataset, China Meteorological Administration) report ~1.4°C–1.47°C. NASA GISTEMP uses 1951-1980 as reference period for anomalies in its main table; the question refers to 'above pre-industrial' which requires additional conversion. The specific NASA GISTEMP No_Smoothing value for 2025 was not released within the resolution window (window closes Jan 11; WMO/NASA release was January 14). The data needed for definitive resolution was not available within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criterion specifically requires the NASA GISTEMP 'No_Smoothing' value for 2025 to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. NASA GISTEMP's 2025 annual data was not published within the resolution window (Dec 30, 2025 – Jan 11, 2026). The WMO's consolidated release including GISTEMP was scheduled for January 14, 2026, after the window closed. Furthermore, multiple credible sources report 2025 global temperature at ~1.47°C (below 1.5°C threshold) while Copernicus ERA5 reports >1.5°C — but these are not the specified resolution source. Since the specific NASA GISTEMP data was not available within the window and cannot be confirmed, and since the window closed before the data was released, this question cannot be definitively resolved within the window. However, since the window ends January 11, 2026, and no qualifying NASA GISTEMP data was released by then, and the broader evidence suggests the value would be ~1.47°C (below threshold) for most datasets, the resolution is effectively No — the condition was not met within the window. The question remains resolvable=false due to missing primary data source.

Some sources use language like 'drops bid' loosely in headlines, but the substantive content is uniformly conditional.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria require formal renouncement of Ukraine's NATO membership bid. question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla publicly release a Full Self-Driving (FSD) capability that operates without a human driver present on public roads before October 1, 2025?

question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and Ukraine finalize and publicly announce a binding defense agreement equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: On August 22, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Andrii Yermak, head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, held discussions on security guarantees for Ukraine. The plan involved political-legal and military groups working on guarantees, including weapons supply, financial support, intelligence sharing, and joint training missions. The draft project of security guarantees was planned to be finalized by the end of next week. Moreover, there have been discussions at global summits, with expectations for the U.S. to provide robust and credible security guarantees to Ukraine. The U.S. has also issued a similar security guarantee to Qatar, which referenced NATO's Article 5, indicating their willingness to provide binding defense obligations. These events provide context for the ongoing discussions and negotiations between the U.S. and Ukraine regarding a potential security agreement.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if credible reports confirm the finalization and public announcement of a binding defense agreement equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment between the U.S. and Ukraine before November 30, 2025. Credible sources for resolution may include major international news agencies, official statements from the U.S. State Department, the Ukrainian government, or other recognized national authorities or declarations.
subquestions.rationale: The question aims to assess the progress of U.S.-Ukraine discussions on security guarantees, specifically focusing on the likelihood of finalizing a binding defense agreement equivalent to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment. The outcome of this question will serve as an early indicator of the likelihood of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The US and Ukraine must have FINALIZED and PUBLICLY ANNOUNCED a BINDING defense agreement equivalent in character to NATO Article 5 (mutual defense commitment) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30. Observable evidence: Official signed agreement, government press releases confirming binding mutual defense obligation. Key threshold: Must be 'binding' and 'equivalent in character' to Article 5 — mere proposals or draft frameworks do not qualify.

Query 5: 'Ukraine US agreement signed finalized binding November 28 29 30 2025' — to check final days of window. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) November 20-21, 2025: US delivered draft peace plan + separate security guarantee document modeled on Article 5 to Ukraine. REJECTED — this is a draft proposal, not a finalized/signed agreement. (2) November 23-24, 2025: Geneva talks between US and Ukraine reached 'common understanding on core terms.' REJECTED — explicitly not a final agreement; security guarantees described as 'unresolved.' (3) November 25, 2025: Ukrainian official Umerov said Ukraine 'agreed to peace deal.' REJECTED — Zelensky himself denied 'deal done' reports; most sensitive issues including security guarantees remained for future Trump-Zelensky direct talks. (4) November 27-30, 2025: Ongoing shuttle diplomacy, Ukrainian delegation sent to US. REJECTED — talks described as continuing into December; Witkoff-Putin meeting in Moscow planned for 'following week.' No finalization occurred.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event within the window satisfies the resolution criteria. The draft US security guarantee document [bne IntelliNews](https://www.intellinews.com/draft-us-security-guarantees-offer-ukraine-article-5-style-protections-axios-412823/) described as 'Article 5-style' was explicitly a draft proposal, not a finalized binding agreement. The [New York Post](https://nypost.com/2025/11/21/world-news/trumps-nato-style-security-deal-offered-to-ukraine-amounts-to-less-than-a-guarantee/) analysis noted it 'falls significantly short of a binding military commitment' since it only required the US president to 'determine appropriate measures' without guaranteed obligation. The Ukrainian Ambassador on CBS News on November 23 described the security document as 'not a formal treaty but a framework similar in spirit to Article 5.' [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/olga-stefanishyna-ukrainian-ambassador-us-face-the-nation-transcript-11-23-2025/). As of November 29, 2025, a Ukrainian delegation was still en route to the US to continue negotiations, with talks 'scheduled for following week' including Zelensky. [The Indian Express](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/zelenskyy-says-ukrainian-delegation-on-its-way-to-us-for-talks-10393111/). evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp for a qualifying event can be extracted because no qualifying event occurred. The closest events were: draft leaked/delivered November 20-21, 2025; 'common understanding' reached November 23-25, 2025 (but not a binding agreement). No finalization or signing occurred before November 30, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the window. The window closed without a binding agreement being finalized or announced.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) Some reports on November 25 claimed Ukraine 'agreed to the peace deal,' but Zelensky personally denied this and described ongoing talks. (2) The European Parliament resolution adopted November 27 explicitly called for security guarantees 'equivalent to Article 5' to be included in any future agreement — demonstrating no such guarantee had been finalized yet. [Azeri Press](https://en.apa.az/europe/european-parliament-adopts-resolution-outlining-eu-demands-for-peace-plan-for-ukraine-484861). (3) Russia's Putin called the plan 'a starting point for future agreements' on November 27, explicitly indicating it was not finalized. (4) Sunday Guardian Live (November 29) summarized the situation as 'peace remains as elusive as the war itself' and 'the plan remains politically contested, with no viable constituency.' (5) The 'Coalition of the Willing' task force formed November 25 was explicitly to 'solidify' security commitments 'in the coming weeks' — proving nothing was finalized during the window. These all confirm no binding agreement was reached.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly and consistently shows that no binding US-Ukraine defense agreement equivalent to NATO Article 5 was finalized or announced during the window (October 31 – November 30, 2025). What occurred was: (1) A draft security guarantee document modeled on Article 5 was proposed/leaked around November 20-21; (2) Negotiations between US and Ukraine progressed but reached only a 'common understanding on core terms' — not a final agreement; (3) Security guarantees remained explicitly unresolved as of the end of the window; (4) Negotiations were continuing into December 2025. subquestions.background_information: Reports indicate that Tesla has launched a robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, as part of a limited and carefully monitored trial. The service includes a small number of Model Y vehicles operated in a geofenced area within the city limits. The vehicles are using Full Self-Driving (FSD) software which is under the supervision of a 'safety monitor' in the front passenger seat. The presence of the safety monitor contradicts Elon Musk's original promise of unsupervised rides. Additionally, there have been regulatory challenges in Texas related to the launch of driverless vehicles, with new laws mandating a permit to operate self-driving vehicles set to take effect on September 1, 2025.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if credible reports confirm the public launch of a fully driverless Tesla robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, without any human actively controlling the vehicle, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08. Resolution will be based on reports from authoritative sources such as major news outlets or official Tesla announcements. Sources: [1] CNA - https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/texas-enacts-robotaxi-rules-eve-tesla-austin-rollout-1551352, [2] Popular Mechanics - https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/a40564133/elon-musk-promised-driverless-taxis-instead-you-get-a-guy-in-the-passenger-seat/
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it specifically focuses on the launch of a fully driverless taxi service in a defined location before the resolution date. The outcome of this subquestion could provide an early indication of Tesla's progress towards achieving a fully driverless robotaxi service, which is crucial for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: A fully driverless Tesla robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, must have launched between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08, with no human actively controlling the vehicle. Observable evidence: credible news reports or official Tesla announcements confirming operation without any human safety monitor or driver in the vehicle. Key entities: Tesla, Austin TX, robotaxi service. Key constraint: 'without any human actively controlling the vehicle.'
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Tesla robotaxi driverless Austin Texas launch 2025' (June–September 2025) — to find launch details; 2. 'Tesla Cybercab fully autonomous taxi service Austin September 2025' (June–September 2025) — to find any September launch; 3. 'Tesla robotaxi fully driverless no safety monitor September 2025 Austin' (Sept 1–8) — to find evidence of fully driverless operation without human onboard; 4. 'Tesla Texas SB 2807 robotaxi safety driver requirement September 2025' (Aug–Sept 2025) — to find regulatory constraints on driverless operation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Tesla robotaxi launched in Austin on June 22, 2025, with safety monitor in passenger seat — prior to window, and NOT fully driverless. (2) As of Sept 1, 2025 (per Benzinga/Teslarati), Tesla moved safety monitors to the driver's seat for highway trips — still has human in vehicle. (3) Sept 4, 2025: Tesla opened public app — but still with safety monitors present. (4) Elon Musk stated safety drivers to remain 'for first few months... should be no safety driver by end of year.' All candidate events within the window show humans present in vehicles. No event found showing operation without any human in the vehicle during Sept 1–8, 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires 'fully driverless... without any human actively controlling the vehicle.' Multiple authoritative sources confirm that during the entire Sept 1–8, 2025 window: [Mashable](https://mashable.com/article/tesla-robotaxi-human-safety-monitor-drivers-seat) (Sept 5): 'Tesla has begun placing human safety monitors in the driver's seat'; [Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/tesla-robotaxi-2000653821) (Sept 5): 'Tesla...remains a Level 2 system that needs constant driver supervision'; [IBD](https://www.investors.com/news/tesla-stock-bulls-driver-seat-robotaxi-safety-monitors/) (Sept 3): 'Tesla's robotaxi fleet in Austin, Texas, now operates with safety drivers because a new Texas law effective Sept. 1 requires a safety driver for vehicles that are not Level 4 or 5 autonomous'; [Cryptopolitan](https://www.cryptopolitan.com/tesla-robotaxi-app-beat-uber-waymo-downloads/) (Sept 5): Musk said safety driver 'should be no safety driver by end of year' — clearly NOT removed within the window; [US Sun](https://www.the-sun.com/motors/15091628/new-driving-laws-september-fines-labor-day/) (Sept 1): 'Tesla's robotaxi in Austin remains exempt [from SB 2807 permit requirement] because it has a human safety monitor.' None of these match the criteria of 'fully driverless without any human actively controlling the vehicle.'
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp could be extracted for a fully driverless (no human in vehicle) Tesla robotaxi operation in Austin during Sept 1–8, 2025, because no such event was reported. The opposite was confirmed: human safety monitors were present throughout the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable — no qualifying event (fully driverless without human) occurred within or before the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Texas SB 2807 (effective Sept 1, 2025) legally mandates a safety driver for Level 2 vehicles like Tesla's FSD system, making a fully driverless operation (without human) legally impossible during this window. Musk himself stated removal of safety drivers as a future goal ('by end of year'). Multiple independent sources (Forbes, CNET, Benzinga, Teslarati, Mashable, Gizmodo, IBD) all consistently confirm human safety monitors were present in Tesla robotaxi vehicles throughout the Sept 1–8 window. No contradictory evidence found suggesting fully driverless (no human) operation occurred.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. During the entire September 1–8, 2025 window, Tesla's robotaxi service in Austin operated with human safety monitors in the vehicle — either in the passenger seat (city routes) or in the driver's seat (highway routes). Texas law (SB 2807, effective Sept 1) required safety drivers for Level 2 vehicles. Elon Musk confirmed safety drivers would remain for months, targeting removal 'by end of year.' No evidence exists of a fully driverless Tesla robotaxi service (without any human in vehicle) in Austin during the window. The condition became definitively unsatisfied as of September 1, 2025, when the new Texas law took effect requiring safety drivers for Level 2 systems like Tesla's FSD, and consistent reporting throughout the window confirmed human presence.

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announce another federal government shutdown by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET?
subquestions.background_information: Recent news articles indicate the possibility of another government shutdown if Congress fails to pass necessary spending bills by the deadline. Bipartisan negotiations and disputes over funding, particularly related to the Affordable Care Act's enhanced subsidies, have raised concerns about a potential lapse in appropriations. The failure to secure funding could result in a federal government shutdown, affecting the functioning of multiple federal agencies.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) officially announces a federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-31. The resolution will use OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/) as the primary source of confirmation.
subquestions.rationale: The announcement of a federal government shutdown by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management would be a crucial early indicator of the likelihood of a government shutdown by January 31, 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: OPM officially announces a federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-29 (inclusive). Observable evidence: OPM Operating Status page showing 'shutdown' status OR news reports of OPM officially announcing a shutdown. Key entities: U.S. OPM, federal government. Window: 2026-01-09T00:00:00Z to 2026-01-29T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'federal government shutdown January 2026 OPM' (2026-01-09 to 2026-01-29) — to find any shutdown announcement within the window; 2) 'US government shutdown lapse appropriations 2026' (2026-01-01 to 2026-01-29) — to find context on shutdown timing; 3) 'OPM operating status shutdown federal employees January 2026' (2026-01-09 to 2026-01-29) — direct OPM-specific search; 4) 'government shutdown January 29 2026 Senate vote funding' (2026-01-29 to 2026-01-31) — to find what happened on/around the window end date; 5) 'Senate passes spending bill averts shutdown January 30 2026' (2026-01-28 to 2026-02-05) — to find outcome; 6) 'government shutdown started February 1 2026 OPM announcement' (2026-01-31 to 2026-02-05) — to establish exact shutdown start date; 7) 'OPM Office of Personnel Management shutdown announcement January 31 2026' (2026-01-30 to 2026-02-03) — OPM-specific announcement search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) On January 29, 2026 (within window): Senate voted 45-55, failing to advance the funding package. No shutdown occurred — negotiations continued. (2) On January 30-31, 2026 (outside window): Senate passed a deal 71-29 late on January 30; the House was in recess; partial shutdown began at 12:01 a.m. ET on Saturday, January 31, 2026. (3) The Cryptopolitan article (published January 31, 2026) explicitly confirms the OPM-based resolution criteria and notes that a Polymarket contract with identical criteria (OPM announcement by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET) would resolve Yes. REJECTED for resolution purposes: The shutdown occurred on January 31, 2026 — OUTSIDE the resolution window which closed January 29, 2026.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires OPM to announce a shutdown between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-29 (per the question's end date parameter). Multiple sources confirm the shutdown began at 12:01 a.m. ET on January 31, 2026 [AP](https://apnews.com/article/government-shutdown-homeland-security-pentagon-transportation-2dd3464f56295ff79f136c1c5c24a532), [TimesNow](https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us/us-news/breaking-us-government-enters-partial-shutdown-as-2026-budget-fails-to-pass-congress-article-153535951), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/heres-what-to-know-about-the-partial-government-shutdown-and-its-impact), [Idaho Capital Sun](https://idahocapitalsun.com/2026/02/01/repub/partial-federal-government-shutdown-begins-amid-hopes-it-wont-last-long/). On January 29, 2026 (the last day in the window), the Senate voted 45-55 to block the funding measure — no shutdown had yet occurred [Gateway Pundit](https://www.thegatewaypundit.com/2026/01/senate-blocks-measure-advance-funding-package-seven-republicans/), [Redstate](https://redstate.com/smoosieq/2026/01/29/new-senate-fails-to-advance-funding-bill-as-partial-shutdown-looms-n2198640). The shutdown did not begin within the January 9–29 window. Criteria: NOT MET within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Shutdown start: 12:01 a.m. ET on January 31, 2026 = 2026-01-31T05:01:00Z. This is OUTSIDE the resolution window (which ends 2026-01-29T23:59:59Z). Within the window, no OPM shutdown announcement was made. The OMB (not OPM) initiated shutdown preparation guidance on January 30, 2026, but this was outside the window and was preparatory guidance, not a shutdown announcement itself.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying OPM shutdown announcement occurred within the January 9–29, 2026 window. The shutdown only began on January 31, 2026. No earlier qualifying event exists within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Some articles describe the shutdown starting 'January 31' and others 'February 1' due to differing conventions (midnight boundary). However, all agree the shutdown started at/after midnight on the January 30-31 boundary — either way, it was OUTSIDE the January 9–29 window. The Cryptopolitan article confirms that even prediction markets using the identical OPM criterion (Polymarket: OPM announcement by January 31 at 11:59 PM ET) showed 99% probability of Yes — meaning OPM did eventually announce a shutdown on January 31. But January 31 is after the resolution window's end date of January 29. There is no evidence of any OPM shutdown announcement within the January 9–29 window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The partial government shutdown began on January 31, 2026, which is AFTER the resolution window closed on January 29, 2026. Within the window (January 9–29), Congress was actively working to prevent a shutdown, and no shutdown occurred. The Senate failed a procedural vote on January 29 but no shutdown resulted that day — negotiations continued into January 30-31. Therefore, the resolution is No: OPM did not announce a government shutdown between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-29. The window closed on January 29, 2026 without a qualifying event, making the resolution definitively No as of 2026-01-29T23:59:59Z.

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The DOL report was released on November 26, 2025 (one day early due to Thanksgiving holiday). evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is only one qualifying event: the DOL report for the week ending November 22, 2025, released on November 26, 2025. This is the first and only occurrence of the relevant data point within the window.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. Department of Labor officially reported 216,000 initial unemployment claims for the week ending November 22, 2025, released on November 26, 2025. question: Will Russia capture Pokrovsk train station by October 31?

subquestions.question: Will the ISW map shade any part of the Pokrovsk train station icon red by October 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The ISW map provides geolocation data on military developments and territorial control in the conflict in Eastern Ukraine. The shading of the Pokrovsk train station icon red on the ISW map would indicate a change in territorial control and potential capture by either Russian or Ukrainian forces. The Pokrovsk train station is strategically located within the Donetsk region, making it a key area of interest amidst the conflict.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves positively if any part of the Pokrovsk train station icon is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by October 20, 2025. subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant as it directly assesses the critical indicator of territorial control within the specified region. The capturing of the Pokrovsk train station by either party would likely precede and influence the ultimate capture of the region, thus providing valuable insight into the progress of the conflict.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The ISW map must shade the Pokrovsk train station icon (a specific map symbol on the ISW ArcGIS story map) red — indicating Russian control of that location — by October 20, 2025. Observable evidence would be: (1) direct ISW map screenshots showing the station icon red, (2) credible reporting that Russian forces captured/controlled the Pokrovsk train station specifically, or (3) DeepState map confirmation of that specific location being Russian-controlled. Key entities: Pokrovsk city, its railway station, ISW map, October 20, 2025 deadline.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Pokrovsk train station Russian forces captured October 2025' — to find direct capture reports. Query 2: Ukrainian language search for Pokrovsk railway station capture October 2025. Query 3: 'ISW Pokrovsk station Russia control October 2025' — to find ISW map updates. Query 4: 'Pokrovsk city center Russian advance urban fighting October 2025' — to find evidence of Russian advance into city center near station. Query 5: 'Pokrovsk railway station Russian occupation DeepState map October 2025' — to check DeepState. Query 6: 'Russians enter central part of Pokrovsk' — to investigate October 19 claims. Query 7: 'ISW Institute for Study of War Pokrovsk red October 2025 territory' — to find ISW map evidence.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) DeepState October 18 reported Russian advances 'in Pokrovsk' — but this is vague and doesn't specify the train station; (2) Medium.com October 19 article about Russian bloggers claiming Russians 'entered central part of Pokrovsk' — explicitly flagged as unsubstantiated, sourcing a non-existent Ukrainian website; (3) ISW October 4 report mentioning Ukrainian forces 'securing positions in southern Pokrovsk'; (4) Ukrainian AFU reports of Russian sabotage groups active inside the city. All rejected as not meeting the specific criteria of the train station icon being shaded red on ISW map. No confirmed report of Russian capture of the Pokrovsk train station was found.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found that specifically matches the resolution criteria. [DeepState, Ukrainska Pravda, Oct 18](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/10/18/8003303/) reported advances 'in Pokrovsk' but this is not specific to the train station and does not indicate ISW map shading. [Medium.com Oct 19](https://medium.com/@ThatGuyNoah/russians-enter-central-part-of-pokrovsk-critical-ukraine-update-10-19-2025-5b64c31c4ff2) explicitly debunks claims of Russians in Pokrovsk city center. [France 24 Oct 17](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20251017-ukraine-visit-a-city-on-the-frontline-with-our-correspondent-on-the-ground) confirmed Russia had 'failed to capture any major towns in 2025.' [UK MoD Oct 16](https://www.newsweek.com/ukraine-war-russia-advances-update-territory-10887749) described Russia as still trying to 'encircle' Pokrovsk, not having captured it. Ukrainian General Staff repeatedly stated fighting is on 'outskirts' of Pokrovsk, with sabotage groups inside but not territorial control. No ISW map update showing the Pokrovsk station icon red was found in any source.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp could be extracted for a qualifying event (Russian control of Pokrovsk train station on ISW map) because no such event was found to have occurred during the resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (ISW map shading Pokrovsk train station red) was found at any point in the October 1-20, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to disprove a 'No' conclusion by searching specifically for Russian capture claims and pro-Kremlin sources. Found October 19 claims from Russian bloggers about entering Pokrovsk's central area — these were explicitly characterized as unsubstantiated propaganda by the reporting source. DeepState's October 18 report of advances 'in Pokrovsk' is consistent with incremental street-level fighting in outer districts, not capture of the city center or train station. Ukraine's military consistently maintained they were 'eliminating' Russian forces on Pokrovsk's outskirts and conducting counter-sabotage within the city. No source cited the ISW map showing the station red. The weight of credible evidence points to Ukrainian control of Pokrovsk city including the train station throughout the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly indicates that Russian forces did NOT capture the Pokrovsk train station during October 1-20, 2025. Ukraine maintained control of Pokrovsk city throughout this period, with fighting limited to outskirts and sabotage group infiltration (not territorial capture). No ISW map update showing the train station icon red was reported. The question resolves No, with the resolution datetime being the end of the resolution window: 2025-10-20T23:59:59Z.

question: Brazil unemployment below 6.3% for Q4 2025?

subquestions.question: Will Brazil's unemployment rate be below 6.2% for the quarter ending October 2025, as reported by IBGE?

Furthermore, various sources indicate positive momentum in Brazil's labor market and record low unemployment rates in recent quarters. These indicate a trend towards a lower unemployment rate, making it relevant to monitor if the trend continues for the October 2025 quarter.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Brazil's unemployment rate for the quarter ending October 2025, as reported by IBGE, is below 6.2%. The resolution will be based on the official public release of the figure by IBGE. Specifically, the data will be obtained from https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego. The publication is expected in January 2026, and if delayed beyond February 28, 2026, the last published figure will be used.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is relevant to the ultimate question as it assesses whether the declining trend in unemployment continues for the quarter ending October 2025, indicating the likelihood of the unemployment rate being below 6.3% for Q4 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Brazil's unemployment rate for the quarter ending October 2025 (August–October 2025), as reported by IBGE via PNAD Contínua, must be below 6.2%. question: Will Iran withdraw from the NPT in 2025?
description:

evidence.step8_final_decision: The Iranian parliament did not approve the NPT withdrawal plan before 2025-10-01. question: Will Trump announce a national housing emergency in 2025?
description:

question: US bank failure by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any US bank fails between November 11 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (according to FDIC's "Failed Bank List"). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Pulaski Savings Bank failure - January 17, 2025 (before window). (2) Santa Anna National Bank failure - June 27, 2025 (before window). (3) Nigerian bank failures (Aso Savings and Loans, Union Homes) - December 15-16, 2025 - REJECTED: these are Nigerian banks regulated by CBN/NDIC, not U.S. FDIC. No candidate events for FDIC-listed U.S. bank failures between December 13, 2025 and January 12, 2026 were found in any search results.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires the FDIC to add a new U.S. bank to its 'Failed Bank List.' Multiple authoritative sources confirm only two U.S. bank failures occurred in all of 2025: Pulaski Savings Bank (January 17, 2025) and Santa Anna National Bank (June 27, 2025), both before the question window. [U.S. News & World Report](https://www.usnews.com/banking/articles/all-the-banks-and-credit-unions-that-failed-in-2025) [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/banking/article/failed-banks-list-225511842.html). (b) The 800 million figure was only announced on October 6, 2025, by Sam Altman at DevDay, per [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/06/sam-altman-says-chatgpt-has-hit-800m-weekly-active-users/) and [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/chatgpt-users-openai-sam-altman-devday-llm-artificial-intelligence-2025-10) — and this is for WEEKLY, not MONTHLY, users. No source confirms 800 million MAU by end of September 2025.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The 800 million user milestone was announced at OpenAI DevDay on October 6, 2025 — confirmed by TechCrunch (published 2025-10-06) and Business Insider (published 2025-10-08). evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first public announcement of ChatGPT reaching 800 million users (weekly) was October 6, 2025, by Sam Altman at OpenAI DevDay. evidence.step7_verification: All September 2025 data consistently shows ~700 million WEEKLY users — not 800 million and not monthly. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. ChatGPT did not reach 800 million monthly active users by end of September 2025. During the resolution window (September 2025), ChatGPT had approximately 700 million WEEKLY active users. The 800 million milestone (weekly users) was only announced on October 6, 2025, after the resolution window closed. Both the metric (weekly vs. monthly) and the timing (post-window) fail to satisfy the resolution criteria.
